facts.present_here: The Crucible Ash Veiler, The Warm Route, The Warm-Cargo Order

gmNotes.text: Rescue rules on Crucible forbid sending a second crew after workers who crossed a closure line. Anyone caught outside the window reaches the paired shelter and waits out the hot interval on its independent clock, or is not reached at all.

Crucible's uplands yield dense clear crystals that cut like ringglass and hold no stable tuning. A cargo bought here as ringglass will not take a tuning, and the substitution only shows when someone tries to sound it.

Everything imported to Crucible descends through orbital yards on lift windows. A missed window leaves medicine, instruments, or passage circling above the settlement that ordered them until the next safe descent.

entities.name: Crucible

entities.description: The Crucible Ash Veiler shapes charged dust into a protective cloak that sheds Crucible heat without fouling a visor.
entities.name: The Crucible Ash Veiler
entities.veilTagline: The Crucible Ash Veiler shapes charged dust into a protective cloak that sheds Crucible heat without fouling a visor.

entities.description: The Crucible-Front Skater is a mineral-finned animal ranging across Crucible and Ashvane. It rides pressure fronts and sheds cutting flakes when cornered.
entities.name: The Crucible-Front Skater
entities.veilTagline: The Crucible-Front Skater rides Crucible pressure fronts on mineral fins and sheds cutting flakes when cornered.

entities.description: Damarat is a Lithren workshop excavation reached from Ithara, with a functioning ancient forming bed and a small camp whose work depends on it.

descriptiveIdentity.setting: A pressure roof covers one terrace of an ancient works; curved offcuts line the warm passage and untouched terraces descend beneath frozen scree.
descriptiveIdentity.activity: Workers make replacement panels while neighbors search for stolen setting bars and take sides over a buyer's offer to remove the bed.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: A thief has attacked an operator; armed guards seek entry to the camp, and old shafts and a surviving trap interrupt routes into the buried terraces.

facts.present_here: The Damarat Opening, The Damarat Removal
facts.active_here: Ilven Sarith, Osen, Tamet, The Ithara Comparative Expedition, Tovin, Ulveth

gmNotes.text: Bringing a damaged container or panel gets it measured for a local replacement. An operator finds a close match among the old settings, but that bar also fits an unopened rack below the camp.
A worker asks the visitors to keep watch while she follows an oil mark from the stripped setting rack. The marks end at a room belonging to someone who publicly opposed the sale.

entities.name: Damarat

entities.description: A picture from Steady Return identified missing bar fourteen at Glasswake after an earlier reseller load left Lithren; another bar remained with the visiting carrier at Damarat.
entities.name: Damarat Bar Identified Inward

entities.description: The Damarat Bed is a working ancient varal at Damarat, forming broad curved panels from supplied stock under a modern drive.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: A wide field of pale ceramic rod ends beneath a dark platen; modern drive cables run across the old floor.
descriptiveIdentity.handling: Shaped bars set rows of rods, and a test sheet reveals their combined contour before a full load is pressed.
descriptiveIdentity.risks: A proud or fractured rod can split stock; unseen linked motion continues beneath the bed, and lifting the machine requires access through occupied flooring.

facts.function: Forms sheet stock across an adjustable nine-meter bed of ceramic rods

gmNotes.text: A request for an unusual shape leads the operators to an unused adjustment bar. A cheap test pressing makes one part of an unfamiliar assembly whose matching pieces may still be in the lower racks.

entities.name: Damarat Bed

entities.description: Excavators repaired the Damarat Bed and demonstrated it on supplied sheet stock.
entities.name: Damarat Bed Repaired

entities.description: The Damarat Opening was the excavation and mechanical repair that brought an ancient forming bed into use at a Lithren workshop in 2433.

facts.participants: Osen, Tamet, The Ithara Comparative Expedition

gmNotes.text: Comparing a find with the Opening's trial sheets reveals the same curve and a repeated dimple. The preserved setting can reproduce the surface, but the original bar sits in a rack beyond the occupied floor.

entities.name: The Damarat Opening

entities.description: The Damarat Removal is the dispute over Ilven Sarith's offer to buy an ancient forming bed and take it away from the Lithren camp that uses it.

facts.participants: Ilven Sarith, Ressa Dorr, Steady Return, Tamet, The Ithara Comparative Expedition, Tovin

gmNotes.text: A carrier offers a polished setting bar as salvage while a bloodied operator searches the neighboring tables for witnesses. The rack number remains visible beneath its new finish.
The person who admits selling the first bar asks for help recovering the others. Exposing her can turn her own neighbors against her before the departing carrier is searched.
Offering to look beyond the camp brings out a picture of bar fourteen aboard a Pell hauler. Workers disagree over sending a negotiator or someone who will simply take it back.

entities.name: The Damarat Removal

entities.description: Ilven's removal offer reached a divided working camp, and survey guards began visiting its freight approach.
entities.name: Damarat Removal Contested

entities.description: Daret Valis is an Iral Expedition rigger at Ithara, loyal to the crews Selven supports and increasingly opposed to using their recovered machinery against other excavators.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: Short dark hair and a permanent pale band where a helmet seal rubs her neck.
descriptiveIdentity.attire: An Iral pressure suit with bright hand-stitched repairs rather than replacement panels.
descriptiveIdentity.tools: A line reel, locking wedges and a small mirror for looking behind a loaded joint.
descriptiveIdentity.manner: Places someone's hand on the part she wants them to understand.
descriptiveIdentity.disposition: Trusts people who return for their crews; will argue with her employer in front of those crews when an order risks them.

facts.specialty: Counterweighted structures and retrieval across broken ground

gmNotes.text: Daret offers reliable rigging and rescue equipment, then asks who will remain at the controls after everyone crosses. She will not leave an occupied approach beneath a release she cannot reach.

entities.name: Daret Valis

entities.description: Daro Venn is a senior route factor of the Pell Freight Assembly and the former Ratter captain who sponsored the Pell Cut array test.

descriptiveIdentity.disposition: Daro deals in particulars — which yard can make the repair, which master will take a hard return load, which crew has spent its tolerance for risk — and defends a past decision sooner than he apologizes for it.

facts.occupation: Senior route factor of the Pell Freight Assembly

gmNotes.text: Route work runs through him, and so does the memory of which yard can repair an old cutter head, which master will take a difficult return load, and which crew has already spent its tolerance for risk. He is at the Glasswake yard five shifts in six and at Pell on the sixth.
He signs each cordon payment before the route council releases ordinary freight accounts, so Assembly business a crew brings queues behind the bill for a boundary he sponsored.

Raising the four-array test gets a defense of remote cutting with isolated clocks and local stop authority rather than an apology. Treating a schedule as more important than a member turns an Assembly meeting hostile, and some of the people in it voted against him.

entities.name: Daro Venn

entities.description: Davan Koralis is Vantara's Chief Experience Officer, a company leader trained in passenger operations and convoy service.

descriptiveIdentity.disposition: Koralis treats any fault mentioned to him — a cold meal, a dead berth light, a missed rescue window — as part of one journey, and writes it against a named manager before he leaves the room.

gmNotes.text: Every port Koralis calls at gets a rescue drill and an open meeting for local pilots attached to the visit, so anyone working that harbor is invited into both before it becomes clear [Vantara](/glass-frontier/entry/vantara) is selling a route.

Mention a fault to him — a cold meal, a dead berth light, a rescue window missed — and it is written against a named Vantara manager before he leaves the room, whether or not the complaint was meant to travel that far.

He takes refundable reservations for a Shear passenger route the [Compact](/glass-frontier/entry/shear-compact) has not approved, names no departure date, and keeps advertising, which sends ticketholders to ask Shear crews and pilots when the ships actually sail.

entities.name: Davan Koralis

entities.description: The Deep Shear is a set of scattered pockets within the Shear where resonance distortion disrupts distance, angle, and volume.

descriptiveIdentity.setting: Scattered pockets in the Shear's interior where the ambient roar suddenly drops away and distance, angle, and volume begin to disagree with the ship's measurements. Ratters call the sudden hush the listen. Distortion deepens by band: unreliable distances in the outer Deep, curving straight lines in the middle, and inner wrecks holding more interior than their hulls permit.
descriptiveIdentity.activity: Small careful Deep-runner flotillas, pooled Pell crews, heavy industrial rigs, beast-hunters, and Conclave-contracted researchers all work the pockets for what nothing else produces: intact pre-Glassfall components, resonance-shifted matter, and Farborn biology. Most working traffic stays in the outer band and trades in stories about the middle one.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: No instrument reports the crossing in time — a Tuner goes still within seconds, and a crew without one learns from disagreeing clocks or a debris mass charted in two places at once. The same volume surveyed twice yields different charts, a pocket can shift bands inside a hundred meters, and more ships are lost here than to any other identifiable hazard.

facts.present_here: The White Interval
facts.active_here: Coremark, Duthrek, Four Shutters, Pell Freight Assembly, The Choir Fragment Flotillas

gmNotes.text: No instrument reports the crossing in time to act on it. A Tuner on the bridge feels the ambient noise withdraw within seconds; a crew without one finds out from clocks that disagree, parallax that stops behaving, or navigation placing the same debris mass in two positions.

Charts stop holding past the outer band. The same volume surveyed twice produces different charts, so a map the players drew an hour ago records one passage rather than the place, and a pocket can go from outer to middle Deep inside a hundred meters.

Testing a recovered Farborn sample beside an active array can give its stored signal a new path. The membrane recovered after an Empty Bearing report repeats a drive-start tone near tuned glass; a crew hearing its own departure tone in the sample room has reason to shut the array down.

entities.name: Deep Shear

entities.description: Delven's Lens is a telescope showing responsive lights at the same arrangement regardless of its bearing, with streets visible through a second instrument.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: An old brass-colored telescope on a low bench, surrounded by chalk marks for a second instrument.
descriptiveIdentity.handling: Observers signal through it and hold the focusing wheel still while receiving a reply.
descriptiveIdentity.risks: A hand beside the tube casts an enormous shadow across the correspondents' view; refocusing changes the spaces between their lights.

facts.function: Reveals a responsive optical field whose apparent scale changes with nearby hands and the focusing wheel

gmNotes.text: A hand resting casually beside the tube darkens several answering streets. One lamp protests while another moves into the new shade.

entities.name: Delven's Lens

entities.description: Deral is a sural mine in Istrava's upland ridge country, where oshrets have trapped workers on platforms above a mineral seep.

descriptiveIdentity.setting: Suspended ore platforms hang above a steaming seep; clear wedges grow through dark wall rock and pale hunters cling beneath the stairs.
descriptiveIdentity.activity: Trapped miners signal the ridge while rescuers, egg collectors and crystal buyers enter by different cuts.
descriptiveIdentity.access: Vehicles use the lower mouth; narrow upper cuts open above the platforms and the eastern waste incline.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: Oshrets brace against continuous rock, their young reach the suspension cables, and hot cutting can split valuable crystal.

facts.function: Extracts large clear sural crystals for instruments and heavy arrays

gmNotes.text: A lamp on an isolated platform answers movement on the ridge. Its bearers lower a food tin containing a drawing of the animals beneath them.
Cutting crystal sends vibrations through the cavern. Adults approach through continuous rock while a young hunter follows the moving tool's cable.

entities.name: Deral

entities.description: Aren recalled Deral's hunters despite their warning; oshrets occupied the stairs and trapped miners on suspended platforms.
entities.name: Deral Detachment Recalled

entities.description: The Deral Hunters are former league soldiers and civilian cavern hunters returning to free the miners their recalled detachment left behind.

descriptiveIdentity.ideology: Bring the living out and leave the workings fit for the miners to reclaim.
descriptiveIdentity.methods: Draw hunters onto hanging nets, cross stone on padded shoes and shoot exposed joints while animals leap.
descriptiveIdentity.presence: Old league coats cut short at the shoulder, wire decoys and scorch-marked shields carried upside down as stretchers.
descriptiveIdentity.attitude: Experienced hands teach volunteers directly; a rescuer who trades a life for a specimen loses their partners.

gmNotes.text: Offering to help gets a weighted sack thrown toward a hanging net. A hunter wants to see how the visitors handle a leap before trusting them beside a living oshret.

entities.name: The Deral Hunters

entities.description: Dern Talish is the Displacement Council's Fourth First Threshold, responsible for Bloom cordons and the crews that maintain them.

descriptiveIdentity.disposition: Talish listens more than she speaks and never raises her voice. She asks a party what it needs and what it can give, works the gap between the two, and accepts water rather than meals from parties whose disputes she may judge.

facts.occupation: Fourth First Threshold of the Displacement Council

gmNotes.text: A containment question anywhere in the mid-drift reaches Talish within a day. She sends a deputy first and comes herself when the deputy's numbers look wrong.

Offer her a meal while seeking an official decision and she takes water instead. Sharing a table is a closeness she does not extend to people she may later have to rule against. She shares private meals with her old colleague Iro Senn.
She answers with figures and gives them freely. Asked how a cordon held, she credits Council procedure and moves on to the next zone.

entities.name: Dern Talish

entities.description: The Displacement Council named Dern Talish its fourth First Threshold in 2432.
entities.name: Dern Talish Becomes First Threshold

entities.description: Dern Talish began her long Gray Line assignment in 2412, rising from perimeter patrol to regional operations lead.
entities.name: Dern Talish Cordon Career

entities.description: Four-year-old Dern Talish was evacuated from Latch during the Silent Bloom in 2378.
entities.name: Dern Talish Evacuated

entities.description: Oram Sells disclosed the hidden elven conflict to Dern Talish at Gray Line in 2432, and she confirmed it through the communication shard.
entities.name: Dern Talish Read In

entities.description: Dern Talish barred three rival convoys from using Gray Line as a staging point during the Bitter Reach in 2415.
entities.name: Dern Talish Turns Back Convoys

entities.description: The Descent at Drail is the hab's 2435 reservoir celebration, with masked ribbon crossings and visiting ensembles.

descriptiveIdentity.marks: Masks, ribbon invitations and crowded food terraces surround an empty reservoir.
descriptiveIdentity.stakes: Rival dancers attempt crossings beyond their rehearsed reach while old partners search for familiar hands.

gmNotes.text: A held silence draws challengers into the air. The musicians watch the catchers, and will abandon a tune to warn a dancer whose partner has moved.

entities.name: The Descent at Drail

entities.description: Detha is an Istravan captain who escaped an absolute command and now works outside occupied Velisar to recover the crew she left inside.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: A heavy brow, closely cropped hair and a pale burn across one forearm.
descriptiveIdentity.attire: A stripped league coat over civilian work clothes.
descriptiveIdentity.tools: A battery wrench and a folded crew list annotated with last known posts.
descriptiveIdentity.manner: Checks whether someone can refuse before asking them to repeat an instruction.
descriptiveIdentity.disposition: Will expose her own earlier arrests when that is what a prospective ally needs to know.

gmNotes.text: Detha offers a route through a battery passage, then recognizes someone she once arrested among the people being rescued.
A plan to reach Aren makes Detha ask who will recover her crew if she stays to attempt succession.

entities.name: Detha

entities.description: Detha resisted an absolute order to surrender a retreating crew and escaped without reaching Aren Talivar.
entities.name: Detha Disobeys

entities.description: Dez Morrn is a Fermata trumpeter and organizer who leads the station's free-jazz opposition to the governing Standards.

descriptiveIdentity.disposition: Dez starts anyone interested on one sustained tone and moves nowhere until every player in the room can name where it came back through the deck. Performers who break something to prove they are serious are expelled on the spot.

facts.occupation: Trumpeter and organizer of Fermata's free-jazz movement

gmNotes.text: Anyone at Fermata with a grievance about the Standards gets invited to a rehearsal in the damped compartments behind the old freight lining. Dez starts newcomers on one sustained tone and will not move on until every player in the room can name where it came back through the deck.

Players who try to prove their commitment by breaking something get expelled on the spot. She bars anyone who plays past a marked weak panel and drops anyone who offers a cracked window as evidence of seriousness.

Both of Dez's arrests sit unresolved in the Session archive, so associating with her carries a charge nobody can define and nobody can dismiss. A party pulled in alongside her waits out the repairs while the room fails to agree on what to call the offense.

entities.name: Dez Morrn

entities.description: Dhurak is the armed raider submarine hunting Tavresh's diving expeditions, identifiable by a damaged drive's acceleration noise.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: A short dark pressure hull carries forward weapons and a deep cargo cradle beneath its belly.
descriptiveIdentity.aboard: A cramped control room overlooks a cargo well large enough for seized instruments and a dismantled diver's boat.
descriptiveIdentity.behavior: Waits beneath tower cover, accelerates toward lifted finds and retreats before repair damage exposes it.

gmNotes.text: Rapid acceleration reveals the damaged drive's signature. The crew can silence it by slowing, at the cost of letting a smaller vessel reach the next tower.

entities.name: Dhurak

entities.description: The Dhurak Company is the submarine crew robbing Tavresh's divers, using superior weapons and concealed approaches beneath the ice.

descriptiveIdentity.ideology: Other crews can do the difficult digging; the Company takes the valuable load once it clears the ruins.
descriptiveIdentity.methods: Listen near working divers, threaten their surface boats and retreat under thick ice with the find.
descriptiveIdentity.presence: An armed pressure hull appears above a lifted object before its divers reach the ice hole.
descriptiveIdentity.attitude: Confident against poor expeditions and reluctant to accept damage requiring exposed repairs.

gmNotes.text: A believable repair threat can make the captain abandon a stolen load. A bluff repeated after the vessel is free makes the crew more willing to destroy the next boat.

entities.name: The Dhurak Company

entities.description: The Disappearance of the Elves is the recognized absence of every elven community and individual when sustained communication returned in 2305.

descriptiveIdentity.marks: Archives across Kaleidos, the ring habs, and the outer worlds carry the same kind of gap: procedures kept and authors lost, decisions preserved with whole departments omitted, named participants replaced by generic descriptions. In the Echo Rivers, conversations cut to silence and voice signatures flatten into harmonic hum. The ring's broad elven history survives; the names, family lines, and locations do not.
descriptiveIdentity.stakes: The Echo Ledger Conclave has not settled whether the pattern records deliberate removal or an unknown failure concentrated around elven signals, and each deep fragment the alteration never reached reopens the argument.

facts.scale: Every publicly known elven community and individual

gmNotes.text: Research into any pre-Glassfall technical procedure turns up a document that still works, full method and full tolerances, with the author line generic or gone. The [Echo Ledger Conclave](/glass-frontier/entry/echo-ledger-conclave) will confirm the gap and will not say whether it was cut out or simply lost.

Listening deep enough in the [Echo Rivers](/glass-frontier/entry/kaleidos-echo-rivers) reaches below the flattening: a conversation that does not cut to hum, carrying a voice signature the alteration never touched. The Conclave catalogs every such fragment, and each one reopens its unsettled argument about the pattern.

Elves stayed in the general population to watch the archives, so research closing on a real elven location gets noticed before it gets published. The interference arrives as a misfiled requisition, a reassigned archivist, or a folio that was on the shelf last visit.

entities.name: Disappearance of the Elves

entities.description: The Displaced-Door Order treats any threshold opening into Xyloathax as occupied housing until inspectors clear it.
entities.name: The Displaced-Door Order
entities.veilTagline: The Displaced-Door Order treats any threshold that opens into Xyloathax as occupied housing until inspected.

entities.description: The Displacement was the mass evacuation of mid-drift ring habitats during the Silent Bloom cascade beginning in 2378.

descriptiveIdentity.marks: Settlements that took refugees keep diaspora quarters where a lost hab's craft, dish, or festival goes on in a place that never had it, and naming a vanished hab as home still carries weight. The Displacement Council draws heavily from these communities, and Bloom-survivor standing holds specific authority in containment work.
descriptiveIdentity.stakes: Families still hire crews toward habs where a relative was recorded as staying behind, and the evacuation records never separated the trapped from those who refused to believe the readings. Everyone alive remembers the evacuation or knows someone who lived it, and the consequences are still arriving.

facts.scale: Tens of thousands evacuated from failing ring habitats

gmNotes.text: Every settlement that took refugees has a diaspora quarter keeping one lost hab's craft, dish, or festival running in a place that never had it. Naming the hab correctly opens doors there; naming it wrong marks the speaker as someone who only read about the evacuation.

A character claiming Bloom-survivor standing is taken at their word by containment crews and handed the reading nobody else can parse. The claim is checkable: survivors know how their own hab failed, and the [Displacement Council](/glass-frontier/entry/displacement-council) recruits from the same communities.

Families still pay crews to run toward habs where a relative was recorded as staying behind, and the evacuation records never separated the trapped from the ones who refused to believe the readings. The hire is for a name confirmed, not a body recovered.

entities.name: Displacement

entities.description: The Displacement Council is a neutral containment order that maintains Bloom Zone cordons and supports displaced communities.

descriptiveIdentity.ideology: Containment before politics: the cordons hold because the Council refused to take sides in the Bitter Reach and still refuses. Displaced communities are owed support, and no one crosses a boundary a crew cannot bring them back from.
descriptiveIdentity.methods: Rotating cordon crews, stillwater damping buoys, and remote cutters worked one boundary section at a time — each with a named operator, an isolated clock, and a stop condition agreed before launch. Funding is voluntary and its influence quiet.
descriptiveIdentity.presence: A thin, disciplined crew at a boundary walk or a cordon office — buoy stores, instruments, and returning crews with damage to report. Its reach is felt more often than seen; most of what the Council does happens where nobody else goes.
descriptiveIdentity.attitude: Neutral to every faction and unbending about procedure. Requests are heard, ranked, and answered with what a stretched roster can actually deliver — which is less than anyone asks.

gmNotes.text: Ask the Council for help and the price is a stop condition agreed before launch: a named field operator, an isolated clock, and a stated point at which the crew turns back whether or not the party is finished.
A Council crew receives casualties from opposing factions at the same cordon. Injured people share its treatment rooms while their companions demand separation, protection, or someone else's removal.

Whenever the party's business would open a second front, the answer costs an existing station its coverage: closed humanitarian offices, longer rotations, smaller cordons left on remote watch. The First Threshold names which.

entities.name: Displacement Council

entities.description: Bloom refugees formed the neutral Displacement Council in 2380 to secure rights, resources, and recognition for displaced communities.
entities.name: Displacement Council Formed

entities.description: The Displacement Council became a standing containment order and took over the Bloom cordons in 2384.
entities.name: Displacement Council Takes Cordons

entities.description: The Dissident adopted a human identity and began teaching practical elven resonance work in 2160.
entities.name: Dissident Begins Teaching

entities.description: The Dissident cleared their room and disappeared in 2180, leaving the Tuner teaching line without its source.
entities.name: Dissident Vanishes

entities.description: Dora Melith is a maintenance worker who cleans the hearing pools at Accord Shore.
entities.name: Dora Melith
entities.veilTagline: Dora Melith cleans Accord hearing pools and pockets the metal petitions that sink before they are read.

entities.description: Ressa's grandmother joined two pressure rooms into an eating hall and supplied independent crews in affordable loads.
entities.name: Dorr Hall Opens

entities.description: Dovra is a low tidal river country on Korvath's middle sea, where shifting channels carry farms and towns toward the port of Lowbank.

descriptiveIdentity.setting: Low tidal river country on Korvath's middle sea, where hundreds of channels divide around wooded islands across a coast wider than some provinces. The shore moves every season — silt closes one mouth, storms open another — and towns stand on rises, old levees, and driven piles, facing water in several directions.
descriptiveIdentity.activity: Family channel barges collect rice, fruit, reeds, and fish from landing stairs and run them to Lowbank, piloted by people who read current color, reed direction, and the tone a pole returns off buried iron sand. Water boards keep thousands of small gates and spillways, and flood labor is compulsory for anyone able to give it.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: A chart a few seasons old routes through channels that are now orchard boundaries. During flood, two gates tuned too closely can answer each other through saturated ground and release together, a pole-thief near the reed banks can fake a convincing bottom strike, and the maze of channels draws smuggled cargo that brings inspections down on honest pilots.

facts.present_here: Dovra Groundsong, The Dovran Holder, The Lowbank Reedwater Household, The Reed Clearing, The Reed Quarantine
facts.active_here: Last Reed, Low Lamp, Lowbank Reed Roll, Mud Bell, Mudhand, The Counterweight, The Reed Exchange

gmNotes.text: Every water board sounds its own registered gate interval at the start of the wet season, so crossing districts changes the note underfoot; children raised near a gatehouse can name their interval and the flood path that goes with it.
Directions in Dovra go stale: a route given by landmark may name a channel silt has since closed, and a chart a few seasons old can run a party into what is now an orchard boundary.

A sealed transit tally proves a cargo crossed inspected water without naming a single channel, so it settles the route and nothing about who loaded the crate; forged tallies appeared within a season of the first issue.

entities.name: Dovra

entities.description: Dovra Groundsong is a vibration that travels through river mud and turns suspended kiln loads toward its source.
entities.name: Dovra Groundsong
entities.veilTagline: Dovra Groundsong is a vibration that travels through river mud and turns suspended kiln loads toward its source.

entities.description: The Dovran Holder keeps a channel barge aligned by matching its vibration through a handrail.
entities.name: The Dovran Holder
entities.veilTagline: The Dovran Holder keeps a channel barge aligned by matching its vibration through a handrail.

entities.description: Drail is a small ring hab whose terraced reservoir becomes a ribbon dance floor before its seasonal filling.

descriptiveIdentity.setting: Homes open onto terraces above a deep white basin crossed by hanging ribbons.
descriptiveIdentity.activity: Residents prepare food, masks and sleeping spaces for the Descent while ensembles rehearse below.
descriptiveIdentity.access: Visiting craft dock at the basin's covered rim; a passenger circuit connects with Fermata Station.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: Weak gravity lengthens a missed catch without bringing the next ribbon within reach.

gmNotes.text: An invitation travels down on a ribbon that was empty a moment earlier. Above it, somebody in a tall painted mask waits for the recipient to look up.

entities.name: Drail

entities.description: Port refusals, lost insurance, and creditor seizures dissolved Drossmark Industries in 2359.
entities.name: Drossmark Dissolved

entities.description: Drossmark Industries was a mid-drift extraction company whose linked heavy cutting arrays caused the Shardfall cascade at Brake.

descriptiveIdentity.ideology: Speed was the product. A buyer paid for a graded load and a delivery window; which claim was cut, with what equipment, and at what loss was Drossmark's business alone.
descriptiveIdentity.methods: Its heavy arrays fixed several debris masses into one temporary field and drew material through all of them without moving the carrier between cuts — quick in open Shear, and passing vibration into every mass the array held. The linked rigs answered to one command, which could keep them all cutting after local crews had tried to stop them.
descriptiveIdentity.presence: Black hull plates bearing three white cuts, a mark that outlasted the company on loaders still working in private yards. Beyond the hulls it survives as a warning: two extraction frames repurposed as sorting tables with their power paths cut, and a Drossmark panel kept in inspection books as the standard picture of linked control.
descriptiveIdentity.attitude: Other people's claims and warnings were priced, not honored. At Shardfall it entered a field the Brake Free Cutters had already marked, fought to hold it, and went on extracting after hab instruments warned that the arrestors were answering its rigs.

gmNotes.text: The black plate with three white cuts still shows on working loaders in private yards, because the hulls outlasted the company by decades. Asking a yard owner where the hull came from is how most people first hear the name.

Proposing to link several cutting arrays under one control gets the Drossmark panel produced from an inspection book. It remains the standard illustration of a command that kept every rig running after local crews had tried to stop them.
Two frames survive at the affected hab as sorting tables with their power paths physically cut. An offer to restore one for extraction has to be made to the people who cut them.

entities.name: Drossmark Industries

entities.description: The Dry Net Breath is a salvager's rumor that warm breath leaves an open vent when someone reads from an unrecovered roll.
entities.name: The Dry Net Breath
entities.veilTagline: Dry Net salvagers leave one vent unsealed because warm breath emerges when crews read from the unrecovered roll.

entities.description: Duthrek is the head of Coremark, directing its extraction cells and convoy crews from Korvath since 2409.

descriptiveIdentity.disposition: Duthrek hears captains in pairs from different units so each can challenge the other's account, and settles their conflicts by protecting the route that will still earn after the present cargo is gone. A concealed failure draws worse from him than the failure itself.

gmNotes.text: Duthrek's quota changes reach the Deep Shear before any explanation does. A crew that worked a zone last season finds it closed or its allowance cut, and the officer carrying the order cannot say whether it followed a Compact survey, a private loss, or a purchase from a cordon crew.

Ask Coremark for a Bloom relic on a settlement's behalf and Duthrek wants the system it will keep running and the name of the person who will hold it. That record sets the price of later access and names the first suspect if the relic moves.

An officer who loses people through an avoidable shortcut can lose the cell's charter, and Duthrek treats a concealed failure worse than the failure. Officers caught short in front of witnesses will bargain hard for a version of events their own crew will repeat.

entities.name: Duthrek

entities.description: Duthrek took sole control of Coremark from Korvath in 2409.
entities.name: Duthrek Takes Coremark

entities.description: The Echo Ledger Conclave is the Sable Crescent archive order that authenticates, interprets, and controls access to records recovered from the Echo Rivers.

descriptiveIdentity.ideology: What the ground remembers must be catalogued, authenticated, and released with its context — because a voice repeated without its provenance can mean anything. An artifact lost is recoverable later; an archivist lost is not.
descriptiveIdentity.methods: Long listening shifts at Echo River surfacing points, written findings sealed and registered at Thornvault, and paid authentication whose assessment carries legal weight under the Tempered Accord. Field cells negotiate, pay, and walk away from an artifact before they will fight for it.
descriptiveIdentity.presence: In the field, a retrieval cell of four to six archivists with packing equipment, careful instruments, a contracted Tuner, and funds; at home, crystal-laced halls built to channel river sound and face the glasslight. The instruments announce the trade.
descriptiveIdentity.attitude: Serious people doing serious work, and priced accordingly. The Conclave answers questions it is paid to answer, guards access to the rest, and has complied with three Accord attempts to force it open in letter while ignoring their spirit.

gmNotes.text: Outside [Sable Crescent](/glass-frontier/entry/sable-crescent) the Conclave arrives as a retrieval cell: four to six archivists with a contracted Tuner, a chartered transport, and the funds to buy the thing the party came for before the party reaches it.
Ask for a record and the answer is a fee and a redaction. The Conclave has three times been ordered to widen access and three times released material technically public and practically useless.

A find of doubtful provenance is worth more once an archivist attests to its resonance signature. The Conclave does not authenticate such goods; individual archivists do it on their own time, which makes the attestation itself something a rival can raise.

entities.name: Echo Ledger Conclave
entities.originBlurb: Archivists catalogue voices from Echo Rivers and govern access to recordings whose context still matters.

entities.description: Echo River listeners formed the Echo Ledger Conclave in 2310 to catalogue records surfacing across Kaleidos.
entities.name: Echo Ledger Conclave Formed

entities.description: Edrath is a retired Istravan walking battery whose armored hull houses Naloven families below guns being reclaimed for Aren Talivar.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: A broad, low armored hull stands on eight splayed legs above white spring terraces; glazed rooms fill the old ammunition galleries.
descriptiveIdentity.aboard: Fruit trees rise through open lifts, washing hangs from traversing rails, and armed sentries occupy the separate upper gun deck.
descriptiveIdentity.behavior: Independent feet probe before taking weight; even a slow turn swings the outer legs through the rooms built beside them.

gmNotes.text: The passage between an upper gun and the engines crosses somebody's home. A household can bar its door while an open ammunition lift offers another approach in view of the sentries.

entities.name: Edrath

entities.description: The Istravan League commissioned Edrath as a walking battery for broken upland ground.
entities.name: Edrath Commissioned

entities.description: Edrath covered Naloven's evacuation into Iridess during an assault on the upland ridge.
entities.name: Edrath Held Naloven

entities.description: Edrath's crew removed its firing assemblies, lowered the battery onto permanent supports and opened its hull to displaced households.
entities.name: Edrath Lowered

entities.description: The Edrath Recall is Aren Talivar's 2435 demand that Naloven surrender its inhabited walking battery and return its surviving crew to league service.

gmNotes.text: An officer can play the recall recording during a negotiation without conveying fresh compulsion. Opening the live receiver to let Aren answer exposes everyone who can hear and understand him to a new command.

entities.name: The Edrath Recall

entities.description: Aren demanded Edrath and its former crew; his recovery party occupied the battery's upper deck at Naloven.
entities.name: Edrath Recalled

entities.description: Edrath's Answer is a recurring ground pulse beneath Naloven, produced when the walking battery's drive feeds through a damaged foot bed into Korvath's iron-bearing stone.

descriptiveIdentity.signs: Water dimples across separate baths at once, hanging cups strike their shelves and the planted foot gives a low metallic answer.
descriptiveIdentity.effects: The driven foot and iron-rich bed form a return path that jolts the hull and shakes brittle mineral shelves.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: A weakened pool rim can fail under a traveler; a gun crew trying to hold aim can keep feeding the movement beneath inhabited rooms.

facts.trigger: Edrath's main drive runs under load with its damaged southern foot connected to the ridge
facts.effect: A shallow structural pulse crosses the bath terraces and returns through the battery's tuned foot, jolting its hull
facts.recurrence: Repeats during loaded engine trials; subsides when the drive is isolated or shut down
facts.mitigation: Lift and isolate the damaged foot, or stop the drive before the returning pulse builds

gmNotes.text: Loading the battery's drive makes cups tap against bath shelves before the hull jolts. A gunner trying to hold aim can keep the drive running while people below scramble away from falling fittings.

entities.name: Edrath's Answer

entities.description: The Eighth Brass Kite is a locator object used between Clearance Eight and Brake. It pulls against the local traffic current to point toward stranded hulls.
entities.name: The Eighth Brass Kite
entities.veilTagline: The Eighth Brass Kite pulls against Clearance's traffic current and points toward stranded hulls.

entities.description: The Eighth Clearance Rule gives disabled vessels the center line at Clearance Eight and Mareth and requires powered craft to yield outward.
entities.name: The Eighth Clearance Rule
entities.veilTagline: The Eighth Clearance Rule gives disabled vessels the center line and makes every powered craft yield outward.

entities.description: Eleven is a settlement of nine thousand people along eleven shafts in the Glass Frontier, sharing one gravity-fed water and coolant line.

descriptiveIdentity.setting: Eleven round courts descend to a water tunnel spaced along six kilometers of service fragment: living quarters on the upper rings, lift machinery in the middle, and a stone-lined gallery at the bottom where the main channel runs. Painted marks show the expected waterline at every bend.
descriptiveIdentity.activity: Neighborhood pumps lift each shaft's share on a daily schedule measured in minutes at a stated valve opening, and the minutes change hands through ordinary bargaining — early water for delivery work, night minutes for repair space. Maintenance workers travel the channel by narrow skiff and raised ledge.
descriptiveIdentity.access: End docks sit on the inner service-fragment circuit between Holl and Vey, with small locks at four of the middle shafts. Between shafts, freight rides an exterior cable and passengers take hab-runners through a parallel bore.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: The line carries machine heat as well as water, so any adjustment at the source reaches the lower shafts as temperature, pressure, and structural tone — a quiet fix upstream announces itself downstream. When the cable is under repair, the water walk becomes the only fast road through all eleven communities.

facts.population_band: About nine thousand residents
facts.role: Water-transfer settlement and maintenance route through a long service fragment
facts.setting: Eleven inhabited shafts spaced along a gravity-fed water and coolant line
facts.access: End docks on the inner service-fragment circuit between Holl and Vey, plus small locks at four middle shafts

gmNotes.text: Freight crosses the shafts on the exterior cable and passengers ride the parallel bore, but with either one down the water walk is the road, and a party travels by skiff through the deep reaches and by ledge past the painted waterline marks.

Water here is bought in minutes at a stated valve opening rather than by volume, and the minutes belong to households and workshops that bargain with them. A crew wanting a bath, a coolant fill, or a wash-down negotiates with a neighbor and usually pays in labor.

Anything adjusted at the source line arrives in all eleven shafts as temperature, pressure, and structural tone, so a quiet fix upstream is known in the lower courts before the party who made it gets there.

entities.name: Eleven

entities.description: The Eleven Olddown is a gravity-following anomaly ranging among Holl, Eleven, and Five Landing. It runs across ceilings when a habitat's gravity changes and drags loose cargo behind it.
entities.name: The Eleven Olddown
entities.veilTagline: The Eleven Olddown runs across ceilings when a habitat's gravity changes and drags loose cargo behind it.

entities.description: The Eleven Scrap Lift is a spoke vehicle serving Eleven, Holl, and Five Landing. It travels on counterweights filled with household scrap.
entities.name: The Eleven Scrap Lift
entities.veilTagline: The Eleven Scrap Lift travels the spoke on counterweights filled with household scrap.

entities.description: Elian died after receiving the Lithren landfall results and before permanent settlement.
entities.name: Elian Dies

entities.description: Elian proposed a planet beyond Vastine and organized repeated positional observations from Pelhari.
entities.name: Elian Outer Planet Hypothesis

entities.description: Repeated images located a moving body along the predicted outer arc.
entities.name: Elian Planet Images

entities.description: Elian Soreth was a Pelhari astronomer whose prediction and observing program led to the documented modern landfall on Lithren.

facts.specialty: Outer-system positional observations

gmNotes.text: Researching an old route turns up Elian's rejected approach beside the successful one. The earlier course passes a surface feature the landing crew never examined; checking it means leaving the familiar route.

entities.name: Elian Soreth

entities.description: No elven community returned to the public network when the Reconnection began in 2305.
entities.name: Elves Vanish

entities.description: The Empty Bearing is the suspected hushmaw reported across three Deep Shear pockets along claim crews' return courses. Recovered membrane repeats one ship's drive-start tone near tuned ringglass.

gmNotes.text: A clean gap returns on the crew's own retreat bearing rather than at one fixed position in ordinary space. Three claim crews have reported it, and the Compact has not declared whether they met one animal.
Repeated active checks strengthen the path a hushmaw follows. Deep-runners vary their retreat checks and carry two decoy resonators after the Empty Bearing appears.
The recovered membrane still repeats the third ship's drive-start tone near tuned ringglass, so testing the only physical evidence reproduces the signal that drew the animal.

entities.name: The Empty Bearing

entities.description: The Empty Fifth is a Five Landing rumor about a bunk key that returns after its guest joins the morning departure queue.
entities.name: The Empty Fifth
entities.veilTagline: Five Landing porters pass around a bunk key that returns to its hook after its guest joins the morning departure queue.

entities.description: Eneth is Anaret's broken suspended workway, carried on sevril bands and counterweighted end frames above a deep machinery court.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: Deck sections float across a dark court on pale bands that catch a sideways lamp; the middle deck lies broken below.
descriptiveIdentity.handling: End frames adjust the supported deck while broad saddles keep its cords from bending sharply.
descriptiveIdentity.risks: A damaged saddle abrades its loaded band, and moving one end changes the reach and clearance of the surviving crossing.

facts.function: Carries people and workpieces between upper workshops on a suspended, adjustable deck

gmNotes.text: Crossing Eneth reveals people working at a lower saddle. They are preparing to remove a valuable band that supports the route above them; the end frame offers a way to take its load elsewhere if it can be reached.

entities.name: Eneth

entities.description: Eris received the Great Restorer after his predecessor completed Ruvian's return and disclosed its preserved loss.
entities.name: Eris Receives Mantle

entities.description: Eris Talven is the current Great Restorer, preparing a composite return at Ithara after receiving the mantle through the disclosed loss of Ruvian's restoration.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: Narrow hands with older workshop scars and a habit of testing the weight of a recovered piece.
descriptiveIdentity.tools: Full-sized joint casts carried beside the original fragments.
descriptiveIdentity.manner: Names an old defect before describing what a return could recover.
descriptiveIdentity.disposition: Wants people to inhabit recovered works again and accepts that deciding which state to return is his responsibility.

facts.specialty: Assembling scattered witnesses into a complete recoverable state

gmNotes.text: Offering Eris a missing witness makes him reassess the whole proposed state, including an old defect the expedition hoped would stay buried.
A patron offers transport on condition that Eris promise a particular return; he asks for help obtaining the evidence before accepting the condition.

entities.name: Eris Talven

entities.description: Eshrel is a storm-scoured tract of Ashvane whose sheltered outcrops mark the known circuit of the moving house Uldevan.

descriptiveIdentity.setting: Low black outcrops interrupt a plain of blowing grit; scratched directions cover their sheltered faces.
descriptiveIdentity.activity: Travellers wait for a moving house or cross between refuges during clear intervals.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: Visibility fails between outcrops, while the Sideways Storm can bend long rigid equipment through a shelter's entrance.

facts.present_here: Sideways Storm

gmNotes.text: Warm window light appears above the grit before any ground is visible. Scratches on the nearest rock show steps on the opposite side of the approaching house.

entities.name: Eshrel

entities.description: The Eshrel Companions are former Uldevan passengers who keep the refuges supplied and seek people still travelling aboard the house.

descriptiveIdentity.ideology: A traveller waiting at an outcrop should find food and somebody's account of the next crossing.
descriptiveIdentity.methods: Compare room sketches, leave folded messages at favored chairs and walk the refuges during clear weather.
descriptiveIdentity.presence: Pocketfuls of folded notes and grit-polished meal tins.
descriptiveIdentity.attitude: Generous with shelter and persistent about companions whose last destination remains uncertain.

gmNotes.text: A Companion recognizes a folded note beside a chair and asks who moved it. It was left in another dining room, addressed to someone still missing.

entities.name: The Eshrel Companions

entities.description: Eveli is Tamet's hand-adjusted varal in Ithara, a contemporary machine making local replacement parts from observations of the Damarat Bed.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: A low bench of pale rods, bright handwheels and a padded platen, with bent trial sheets hanging from its frame.
descriptiveIdentity.handling: Two people can set its exposed screws while another checks the contour with a paddle or sample part.
descriptiveIdentity.risks: Rods set by eye can repeat a hidden flaw in the sample; the platen can trap a hand left between the bed and stock.

facts.function: Forms small covers, bowls and suit plates from supplied stock

gmNotes.text: A newly made cover fits while its case is empty and jams when the owner replaces the load. Tamet asks the owner to keep it filled while an apprentice feels for the point where Eveli copied the damage.

entities.name: Eveli

entities.description: The Evran Company is Ladderwell's association of fighting teachers and former champions, responsible for lending Arev at the court.

descriptiveIdentity.ideology: A borrowed advantage should be exposed to an opponent who understands it.
descriptiveIdentity.methods: Teach counters, pair unfamiliar fighters with experienced partners and compare wearers' recollections between bouts.
descriptiveIdentity.presence: Former champions sitting among the spectators with sand still on their cuffs.
descriptiveIdentity.attitude: Proud of students who beat the harness and curious about skills that remain after it is removed.

gmNotes.text: A teacher recognizes a dangerous transition before a novice wearer does and steps onto the sand, accepting an interrupted exhibition to protect the opponent's arm.

entities.name: The Evran Company

entities.description: Evran Court is a fighting court on Ladderwell's lower bench, home to open bouts and exhibitions in the harness Arev.

descriptiveIdentity.setting: A sunken sand court sits beneath tiered wooden benches, with a harness suspended above the fighters' entrance.
descriptiveIdentity.activity: Open challenges alternate with harness exhibitions and lessons from former champions.
descriptiveIdentity.access: Market stairs descend from Ladderwell's lower streets directly into the spectators' benches.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: A fighter can perform an unfamiliar hold faster than they understand its release.

gmNotes.text: A returning champion stops at the entrance to search the standing spectators. Someone above offers the unfamiliar salute before the champion has put on the harness.

entities.name: Evran Court

entities.description: The Exchange C Rattle Tug is a market cargo vehicle used around Carom, Exchange C, and Wash Four. It moves containers by locking each frame to the habitat's changing spin.
entities.name: The Exchange C Rattle Tug
entities.veilTagline: The Exchange C Rattle Tug moves market containers by locking their frames to the habitat's changing spin.

entities.description: The Exchange C Tally Bowl holds Rattle tally dust sourced from Bay Thirty-One and Exchange C. It settles into the last registered weight of any container opened above it.
entities.name: The Exchange C Tally Bowl
entities.veilTagline: The Exchange C Tally Bowl settles into the last registered weight of any container opened above it.

entities.description: Far Bell is the outer traffic marker for Karet-3, beyond Outside's inhabited platform and clear of the Bloom cordon's working space.

descriptiveIdentity.setting: A truss anchored to an evacuated freight tank beyond the inhabited platform at Outside: a dock frame for one small vessel, two shelter rooms with no passage between them, and a thick oval ringglass plate in a ceramic rim. No beacon repeats here — the station is silent except when the plate gives its single stroke. Cargo tallies, Karet family names, and contractors' warnings cover the shelter walls.
descriptiveIdentity.activity: Arrivals hold and listen; departures stop to shed the cordon's local marks, sealing boundary instruments into transfer cases and taking a clean route strip from the shelter locker. Council workers come out regularly to inspect everything and rewind the striker by hand, since the plate sounds once and cannot sound again until reset.
descriptiveIdentity.access: One stroke through the hull means approach on the route sent with it; silence means hold and query Outside by burst; a second stroke in the same arrival is false. Larger ships stand off and transfer by line or flitter, no cargo opens here, and waiting visitors are tolerated only while a vessel supplies them and vouches for immediate departure in a closure.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: The divided shelters mean a split party is out of each other's reach, and either room can lose pressure and release on its own. The last two reset crews found narrow bare footprints in the dust, crossing both ceramic breaks and stopping under the striker — the Council now sends pairs from separate rooms and photographs the dust before anyone touches the spring.

gmNotes.text: Every arrival at Karet-3 stops here first. One stroke through the hull means approach on the route sent with it, silence means hold and ask [Outside](/glass-frontier/entry/outside) by burst, and a second stroke in the same arrival is false.
Wanting the approach kept open means winding the spring yourself, inspecting plate, dock, and both rooms, and finding out what has crossed the dust since the last crew came out.
The two shelter rooms have no door between them. Split a waiting party and each half is out of the other's reach, and either room can lose pressure and release on its own.

entities.name: Far Bell

entities.description: Far Bell Black Book is a beacon record shared among Far Bell, Outside, and Karet-3. It lists replies received after their registered senders were lost.
entities.name: Far Bell Black Book
entities.veilTagline: Far Bell's black book lists the beacon replies that arrived after their registered senders were lost.

entities.description: Far Bell Ravel Tides are periodic force shifts that draw loose objects toward the next active signal relay before releasing them together.
entities.name: Far Bell Ravel Tides
entities.veilTagline: Far Bell Ravel Tides are periodic force shifts that draw loose objects toward the next active signal relay before releasing them together.

entities.description: The Far Witness is a mantle of the Three that carries Witnessing across centuries of consequences and Elsewhere across any present distance in Kaleidos.

descriptiveIdentity.signs: Old light and sound return through present surfaces, the bearer's eyes answer another place, and people or machines along the trace receive the bearer's face or pulse in return.
descriptiveIdentity.effect: The mantle extends EREFwitnessing|Witnessing||END through system-wide chains of consequence and EREFelsewhere|Elsewhere||END beyond the ordinary spell's single anchored viewpoint.
descriptiveIdentity.limits: Historical work requires a surviving consequence; present observation requires a known live anchor. Neither supplies private intent, an unrealized future, or perception without an answering trace.

facts.qualification: Answers someone who placed dangerous evidence in a public record together with the fact that implicated them
facts.succession: Passes when the bearer deliberately closes their perception and entrusts an unfinished line of evidence to another witness
facts.cost: Observation is reciprocal: people, machines, and resonant presences along a distant or historical trace can perceive the bearer and follow the evidence back toward them

gmNotes.text: When the group examines an object, body, place, or signal that participated in an event, the Far Witness can recover sensory evidence and follow any surviving consequence onward from it.
Distant observation is reciprocal: a person sees the bearer in reflection, a machine logs their pulse, and another resonance reader can follow the same trace back to the bearer and everyone nearby.

entities.name: The Far Witness

entities.description: Survivors gathered around a powered bar on Fermata's fragment in 2140 and began settling shared decisions through its band's call-and-response practice.
entities.name: Fermata Founded

entities.description: The Signal Famine sealed Fermata from the ring and surface in 2160, leaving its musical governance to develop in isolation.
entities.name: Fermata Sealed By Famine

entities.description: Fermata Station is a ring habitat around Kaleidos where public jazz Sessions produce binding civic decisions.

descriptiveIdentity.setting: A ring hab in a quiet orbit of Kaleidos, its ringglass lattice tuned by generations of continuous music. Low sustained tones from the Drone run under everything, and the pulse in the central hall sets the pace the whole station keeps.
descriptiveIdentity.activity: Players trade themes in the public hall while the Audience listens and marks who is absent, and the Drone holds its post around the clock because the chord voicings are load-bearing.
descriptiveIdentity.access: Anyone may listen to a Session. A contested request reaches the ensemble through a Player who has passed the Sit-In. During the annual Open, visiting musicians can join the performance while resident Players retain the vote and the Chair.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: Unresolved harmonic tension stresses the structure itself: a bad hour of playing crazes a window, and a loud coordinated dissonance can move bulkheads or breach a hull. Should the Drone ever stop, bulkheads fail.

gmNotes.text: A disputed request reaches the public hall in a Player's repertoire. The Chair restates its consequence before the first tune, and a familiar ending can commit the room to terms a visiting petitioner has never heard played before.

Outside Open week, a visitor needs a resident Player to carry a proposal into the ensemble. During the Open the visitor can play directly, while the vote and final resolution remain with the residents.

A sustained tone reaches a chalk-marked panel and the door begins binding in its frame. Drone crews need that compartment quiet even when the performance is approaching the resolution everyone came to hear.

entities.name: Fermata Station
entities.originBlurb: A ring hab where public Sessions turn musical improvisation into binding civic decisions.

entities.description: The Fermata Working Ensemble claims a repeated machine tone as public music once three crews can keep time with it.
entities.name: The Fermata Working Ensemble
entities.veilTagline: The Fermata Working Ensemble claims a repeated machine tone as public music once three crews can keep time with it.

entities.description: The First Clean Plate is a Pell-maintained wurm-bit built around the first intact mouth plate shed by the Stockpile Colony. Ratters use its marked yoke to grade later plates and train remote-cutter operators.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: A small clean glasswurm mouth plate in a forked yoke, with witness wires and Pell response marks cut along both arms.
descriptiveIdentity.handling: The operator opens a shallow notch and follows the witness wires as the plate turns toward the clearest material boundary. The Assembly opens and cleans it after every demonstration.
descriptiveIdentity.risks: Locking the yoke sends every change in the seam into the plate. Its repeated bite can also draw a living glasswurm through connected debris.

facts.function: Follows curved mineral and ringglass seams with a mounted glasswurm mouth plate

gmNotes.text: The First Clean Plate is brought out when a disputed bit must be compared with the marked Pell response.
Locking its yoke for a straight cut turns the reference tool into the clearest repeated feeding signal a glasswurm can follow.
Every demonstration consumes wear on the one plate used to authenticate the growing market in replacements.

entities.name: The First Clean Plate

entities.description: The Pell Freight Assembly and six Deep-runner flotillas petitioned the Shear Compact for Deep-specific safety rules in 2420.
entities.name: First Petition For Deep Specific Regulation

entities.description: The First Repeatable Kite Tuning was recorded in 2235 when a freight crew crossed a dry Kaleidos basin with a kinetic array fixed to three cloth spars. Its maintenance record let workshops reproduce the engine within the year.

descriptiveIdentity.marks: Three cloth spars around a kinetic ringglass array and the surviving maintenance record copied by surface workshops.
descriptiveIdentity.stakes: The record made one freight crew's tuning reproducible and turned a local crossing machine into the motive engine used throughout Kaleidos.

gmNotes.text: Any argument about who owns an early kite design eventually reaches the surviving maintenance record, whose copies differ in the marks attributed to the freight crew.
Comparing an early copy with a modern engine exposes which changes were repairs, which became standards, and which workshop later claimed as inventions.
The record proves repeatability, not the identity of the person who found the tuning, leaving every later ownership claim attached to an anonymous working crew.

entities.name: The First Repeatable Kite Tuning

entities.description: A freight crew recorded the first kite tuning another workshop could reproduce.
entities.name: First Repeatable Kite Tuning Recorded

entities.description: Five Bolts is a compact tow vessel working Brake's outer capture lane and cutting lots. Its kinetic array cancels small changes in motion while a mechanical yoke carries one derelict hull at a time.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: A compact tow vessel whose cabin frame is pierced by five oversized fasteners — the bolts holding the arrestor yoke from Brake's first captured derelict. Their heads carry fresh paint, renewed by every crew before a new tow.
descriptiveIdentity.aboard: A three-person cabin built around that yoke. Whoever rides along paints the bolt heads with the crew, because the line does not go on until all five are done.
descriptiveIdentity.behavior: It carries one hull at a time between Brake's outer capture lane and the cutting lots: the kinetic array cancels the small changes in motion while the mechanical yoke takes the pull, so line crews read a steady load through an anchor. One tow frame, one line — anything else that needs shifting waits.

facts.capacity: Three crew and one short-haul tow frame

gmNotes.text: Hulls move between Brake's outer capture lane and the cutting lots on Five Bolts, and with three crew and a single tow frame it works one line at a time. Whatever else needs shifting waits.
No crew takes a new tow until the five oversized fastener heads through the cabin frame have been repainted, and anyone riding along paints with them. The line does not go on until it is done.

Five Bolts holds the captured medical hull beside [Forty](/glass-frontier/entry/forty) with a crew that changes every six hours, so anything arranged on the line has to be arranged again with the next watch.

entities.name: Five Bolts

entities.description: Five Landing is the broad central deck in Holl where five vertical and cross-wall routes meet above a shifting market.

descriptiveIdentity.setting: The broadest continuous deck in Holl, floored with colored bands that run from each of its five routes out through the crowd. Freight sits in the center under a traveling hoist; food stalls, repair tables, and water taps line the wall; removable benches ride the outer rail between lift loads.
descriptiveIdentity.activity: Market trade, freight handling, and public meetings share the floor by turns, and lately survey crews and curious residents stream through on the temporary stair to the chamber above, under awnings the sellers have already staked over unpainted floor.
descriptiveIdentity.access: Five ways in, each with its band: the upper cargo lift, two spring-level ladders, the lower cable gallery, and the narrow bridge across the open wall. Following the wrong color delivers you somewhere else entirely.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: When the hoist operator rings the bell the outer rail clears for a lift load — benches off, meetings stopped mid-sentence, business pushed to the water taps until the freight is down. The new stair lands beside the blue route on floor no band has been painted across.

gmNotes.text: Directions on this deck are colors, not turns — each of the five routes runs its band across the floor and through the crowd. Follow the wrong band and you arrive at the upper cargo lift instead of the spring-level ladders.

The hoist operator's bell clears the outer rail for a lift load. Benches come off, a public meeting stops where it stands, and whatever was being negotiated moves to the water taps along the wall until the freight is down.

The temporary stair from the upper pressure door lands beside the blue route, so the deck now holds survey crews, residents going up to see the chamber, and market awnings already staked over floor nobody has painted a band across.

entities.name: Five Landing

entities.description: Five Landing Empty-Berth Fever is a social condition among stranded passengers who occupy unused rooms and defend them as inherited homes.
entities.name: Five Landing Empty-Berth Fever
entities.veilTagline: Five Landing Empty-Berth Fever is a social condition among stranded passengers who occupy unused rooms and defend them as inherited homes.

entities.description: Five Rooms is a passenger kite serving Mareth, Holl, Vey, and Carom. Its cabins rotate to match the gravity at each destination.
entities.name: Five Rooms
entities.veilTagline: Five Rooms is a passenger kite whose cabins rotate to match the gravity of each destination.

entities.description: The Folded Annex is a ring-era archive and experimental suite in Sithari's deep Underlayers, built from rooms joined through structural resonance.

descriptiveIdentity.setting: A buried ring-era archive deep in the Underlayers: an entry hall, two record galleries, and an instrument well that keep their internal arrangement while their position against the city does not. Gallery windows look into test rooms across distances larger than the complex, cabinet fronts show instruments that still move, and the licensed way in is a reinforced descent gate below the Old Campus service level.
descriptiveIdentity.activity: Licensed parties work slowly: passive reflectors set at every turn and compared by sight, records copied where they lie, loose objects numbered for a later permit, and each member checking a plain wound clock against the others before any new door.
descriptiveIdentity.access: The gate opens only while the surrounding field sits in a narrow range; at other times it faces a shallow recess of blank stone, permits or no permits. A party must include a route surveyor, a certified Tuner, and an archive specialist, and nothing leaves on the visit it was found.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: The Annex has never hurt a crew by violence or collapse — it takes the route instead. Once return indicators diverge, a person can stay visible through a window while no adjacent door reaches them; repeaters have answered from galleries they had not been carried to, and three informal entrants remain missing.

facts.holdings: Ring-era spatial calibration records, test rooms and sealed instrument stores

gmNotes.text: The licensed gate below the Old Campus service level opens only while the surrounding field sits in its narrow range; the rest of the time it shows a shallow utility recess faced in blank stone. A party can arrive on schedule with valid permits and find no Annex to enter.

Whatever a party finds stays where it is. Records are copied in place, loose objects are numbered, and a separate permit names what may be lifted on a later visit, a rule written after a crystal gauge came out of a cabinet and the route used to reach it never appeared again.

Everyone carries a wound clock, and more than a minute of disagreement between them ends the visit at the next door. Push past that and nothing attacks: the place takes the route instead, leaving a person visible through a gallery window and unreachable from the door beside it.

entities.name: The Folded Annex

entities.description: The Folded Annex Corner-Spider is a spatial anomaly ranging between the Folded Annex and Underlayers. It stitches nearby corners together and retreats through the resulting seam when disturbed.
entities.name: The Folded Annex Corner-Spider
entities.veilTagline: The Folded Annex Corner-Spider stitches two nearby corners together and retreats through the seam when disturbed.

entities.description: Forty is Brake's largest enclosed cutting bay, built to divide captured vessels among clean work, hot cutting, quarantine, and cargo recovery.

descriptiveIdentity.setting: Brake's largest enclosed cutting bay, named for the salvage grid painted across the central fragment. Two pressure doors open around a complete small vessel, movable walls carve the interior into clean work, hot cutting, quarantine, and recovered cargo, and overhead rails carry tools and sealed observation cabins above floor anchors that take a hull in nearly any orientation.
descriptiveIdentity.activity: Hulls too dangerous to open in the clear come through here — leaking, contaminated, or still under power — and the bay crew's first question is which way up the vessel should sit before the walls close around it. The captured medical vessel outside the main doors has made Forty its supply lock and clinical staging area.
descriptiveIdentity.access: The crew that brings a hull in follows it through the pressure doors. Inside, movement means the orange floor paths, which stay clear of the traveling wall sections and run to the independent shelters at both ends.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: The walls move: the room a job starts in is not the room it ends in, and the marked paths lead to the shelters rather than back to the doors anyone came in by.

facts.function: Enclosed cutting, quarantine, and live-system access for captured vessels

gmNotes.text: Forty takes whatever Brake captures that cannot be opened in the clear: a hull found leaking, contaminated, or still under power is rerouted into the enclosed bay, and the crew that brought it in follows it through the pressure doors.

The bay crew's first question about a new hull is which way up it should sit. The floor anchors accept almost any orientation, and the movable walls are then set around the vessel into clean work, hot cutting, quarantine, and recovered cargo.

The room a scene starts in is not the room it ends in, because Forty's walls move. The orange floor paths stay clear of them and lead to the independent shelters at both ends rather than back to the doors people came in by.

entities.name: Forty

entities.description: The Four-Hatch Order keeps one docking mouth clear at every Keel stop for unpowered rescue craft.
entities.name: The Four-Hatch Order
entities.veilTagline: The Four-Hatch Order keeps one docking mouth clear at each Keel stop for unpowered rescue craft.

entities.description: Four Shutters is a Pell Assembly claim rig working Deep Shear seams with four isolated receivers and unmanned cutters. Its repeatedly rebuilt process deck supplied the isolation pattern later used aboard Quiet Measure.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: A converted cargo hull with four cutter cradles and four heavy receiving shutters, each surrounded by mismatched plates from a different repair.
descriptiveIdentity.aboard: Painted deck routes separate the four receivers from the bridge and cabins. Every room has its own clock, breaker, hand wheel, and physical tally naming who may reopen it.
descriptiveIdentity.behavior: Four Shutters stands off from a claim while its cutters work. Each return is isolated, sounded, and sampled before the crew opens anything toward the clean end of the vessel.

facts.capacity: Eight crew, four remote cutters, and four isolated receiving rooms

gmNotes.text: A berth master reads Four Shutters by its repairs: each mismatched plate and relocated breaker records something the original layout failed to contain.
Opening a receiver requires the named crew member at its hand wheel; a powered safe reading never substitutes for the tally beside the shutter.
Once a live return enters one room, all eight crew are fixed to stations and any task needing spare hands leaves another control unattended.

entities.name: Four Shutters

entities.description: Four-Span Mutual is a route-aid society that caches food, cable, and relay glass at four surviving stations.
entities.name: Four-Span Mutual
entities.veilTagline: Four-Span Mutual keeps food, cable, and spare relay glass cached at every surviving station on its route.

facts.sources: Blue Step Works, Forty, The Dry Net, Three Arms Yard

entities.name: The Four-Yard Pitch Batch
entities.veilTagline: The Four-Yard Pitch Batch hardens around moving ringglass and peels away cleanly when the vibration stops.

entities.name: The Fourth Bell Company
entities.veilTagline: The Fourth Bell Company is one group of travelers lodged under the Bellward custom who repay a household by carrying one message onward toward Sithari or the Keel.

entities.name: The Fourth Bell Fall
entities.veilTagline: Fourth Bell House lost its upper stair during a Keel vibration and sheltered the trapped guests inside its bell chamber.
