entities.description: Rainline is a narrow Prismwell survey kite built to enter the leading edge of Glassfall showers. Its flank sounders, marker lamps, and sample frame find where a forecast stops being true.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: A narrow survey kite of three separate rings joined by flexible spars, with field sounders along both flanks, disposable marker lamps under the keel, and a folded catch frame behind the cabin. The rebuilt port spar shows in every Glasswake yard: a pale laminated brace crossing the darker original frame like a bone set under the skin.
descriptiveIdentity.aboard: Level is unreliable — seats, lockers, and instrument faces follow different rings, colored bands mark which ring carries each fitting, and a dropped tool can seem to roll uphill when two frames correct against each other. Everyone clips in before the first turn, and hard corrections draw a low creak from the repaired spar through the cabin.
descriptiveIdentity.behavior: It enters below a Glassfall shower's forecast path and climbs until fine grains strike the forward cloth, each ring correcting its own motion so the hull yields where debris pushes hardest. Marker lamps drop behind it at every useful change, leaving a string later vessels use as a temporary lane. The sample frame opens only on the retreat leg, and a full catch gets cut loose before it is allowed to slow the withdrawal.

facts.capacity: Seven crew, two observers, a marker rack, and one folded shower-catch frame

gmNotes.text: Anyone new aboard is clipped in before the first turn and told to read the colored band around a doorway before stepping through it, because seats, lockers, and instrument faces belong to three separately correcting rings. Dropped gear can appear to roll uphill.

An observer who reports what the hull is physically taking against what the field sounders read can change the published forecast, and the divergence counts even when the instruments still agree with one another. The crew expects that call made out loud.

The sample frame opens only on the retreat leg, and the crew cuts a full catch loose rather than spend the seconds needed to close it. Anyone aboard who has paid for material, or whose plan needs the sample, discovers this with the front already moving.

entities.name: Rainline

entities.description: Rattle is Carom's largest sorting deck, where six marked routes distribute cargo and passengers from a Ring Age transfer drum.

descriptiveIdentity.setting: Carom's largest sorting deck, six floor colors radiating from the unloading lane toward neighborhood tables, cold lockers, meal racks, and the drum queue. 'Exchange C' is still painted over the main doors from the Ring Age drum, and the correction wall of misdelivery cards covers the passage to the cold lockers.
descriptiveIdentity.activity: The deck is loud through every alignment: frame wheels striking the expansion gaps, drum bells calling five minutes, two minutes, and closure, couriers shouting route changes across the colored bands while residents line the outer rail waiting on hand delivery — and watching everything in the lanes.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: Ordinary conversation is impossible; talk is shouted or taken into the cold-locker passage. Parcels do go wrong — the oldest card on the correction wall tracks one across all three segments nineteen times before it reached a room beside the deck it started from.

gmNotes.text: Frame wheels over the expansion gaps, drum bells at five minutes, two minutes and closure, and couriers calling changes across the colored bands mean any conversation on the deck is shouted or moved into the cold-locker passage.
Residents waiting for hand delivery stand along the outer rail with nothing to do but watch the unloading lane, which makes them witnesses to whatever happens in the six colored bands.

Asking after a parcel that went astray gets a party sent to the correction wall, whose oldest surviving card follows one across all three segments nineteen times to a room beside the exchange it started in.

entities.name: Rattle

entities.description: Rattle Bench is a civic claims body serving Exchange C and Carom, with hearings held around the sealed disputed cargo.
entities.name: Rattle Bench
entities.veilTagline: Rattle Bench settles damaged-cargo claims in public while the disputed container remains sealed between the parties.

entities.description: The Rattle Founding Years began when Wash workshops moved their weighing benches into Carom's open market.
entities.name: Rattle Founding Years
entities.veilTagline: Rattle Founding Years began when Wash workshops moved their weighing benches into Carom's open market.

entities.description: The Rattle Sorter is a cargo machine used at Exchange C, Carom, and Wash Four. It separates goods by resonance and rejects unregistered sealed boxes onto the public floor.
entities.name: The Rattle Sorter
entities.veilTagline: The Rattle Sorter separates cargo by resonance and throws any unregistered sealed box onto the public floor.

entities.description: Ravel is a settlement of thirty-five hundred people on a small ring fragment in the Glass Frontier, harvesting a mineral-rich plume every nine days.

descriptiveIdentity.setting: A small fragment with twelve booms extending like narrow bridge arms, fine mesh spanning the gaps during a catch and larger salvage nets trailing beyond the frame. Habitation shelters behind a thick central shield, and the sideways windows show the plume arriving as a pale band against the stars.
descriptiveIdentity.activity: Life runs on the nine-day plume cycle: two days of line inspection and mesh repair, then the catch with boom crews in paired cabins watching strain beside resonance readings, then open days of processing, anchor tests, and mesh recovery by tender.
descriptiveIdentity.access: A short Keel branch aboard Nera Doss, or a chartered tender, reaches the one sheltered dock behind the fragment.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: A damaged net can drag a boom out of alignment, so when strain crosses the red mark the crews release the whole panel — and with it somebody's inherited share, drifting in the plume until a tender brings it back.

facts.population_band: About thirty-five hundred residents
facts.role: Volatile and ice collection from a recurring orbital plume
facts.setting: A small fragment carrying woven collectors across a broad plume passage
facts.access: Short Keel branch aboard Nera Doss or a chartered tender to one sheltered dock behind the fragment

gmNotes.text: The nine-day plume cycle decides what anyone can get out of Ravel. In the two days before a passage every hand is on line inspection and mesh repair, and during the open days the tender crews are out among the released panels rather than at the dock.

Players who offer to buy, salvage, or claim a collector panel find that its owner stripe and edge repair marks are the ownership record, and that the family holding shares in it reads the last ten yields before naming a price.

A struggle, an accident, or an improvised maneuver out on the web during a catch pushes a boom past its red strain mark, and the crews answer by releasing the whole panel. Someone's inherited share then drifts into the plume until a tender recovers it.

entities.name: Ravel

entities.description: Ravel Lean was the season when Noll root cable held Ravel together through repeated spin loss.
entities.name: Ravel Lean
entities.veilTagline: Ravel Lean names the season when Noll root cable held the habitat together through repeated spin loss.

entities.description: Ravel Underturn is the settlement's recurrent inversion field, exchanging equal volumes from strata with matching resonant loads while leaving every intervening layer untouched.

descriptiveIdentity.signs: Two separated strata fall silent on signal together and appear on instruments at both positions before their equal volumes exchange.
descriptiveIdentity.effects: Each volume arrives in the other's position with rooms, atmosphere, heat, momentum, broadcasts, and living bodies intact.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: Present traffic can descend into stone while a buried ruin's pressure, poison, inhabitants, and unfinished motion resume at the surface.

facts.trigger: Two separated strata carry matching resonant loads when the inversion field reaches its reversal point
facts.effect: Equal volumes exchange position without crossing the intervening matter, carrying structures, atmosphere, heat, momentum, signals, and living bodies intact
facts.recurrence: One field follows Ravel's plume cycle and is recognized elsewhere by paired signal silence, duplicated instrument positions, and an exact exchange of volume
facts.ending: The exchange completes when both volumes settle into the other's resonant load; changing either load during transit arrests both volumes between positions
facts.mitigation: Keep inhabited and buried strata deliberately unequal in load, isolate dangerous layers, and evacuate both paired positions when signal silence begins
facts.anchor_behavior: Pairs volumes by resonant load rather than separation, material, ownership, or local gravity
facts.medium: Layered terrain, ring decks, buried structures, atmosphere, fluid, and signal-bearing matter
facts.content: Two equal volumes with all structures, substances, signals, momentum, and living bodies present inside them
facts.hazard: An inhabited layer can exchange with sealed wreckage, poison, hostile life, old transmissions, or another occupied volume whose motion resumes on arrival

gmNotes.text: Paired signal silence marks two equal loads beginning to exchange, so protecting the occupied layer requires preparing the ruin, poison, wreckage, open void, or living ground that will arrive in its place.

entities.name: Ravel Underturn

entities.description: Ravel Water is a warm resonant condensate collected from Ravel's outer nets and held in six separated trays because nearby samples pull themselves together.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: A clear liquid in six sealed trays, warm to the room and still fluid at temperatures that freeze ordinary water beside it. It carries the plume's mineral salts and a chain of complex carbon compounds no earlier catch contained.
descriptiveIdentity.working: Handling is separation: pressure cells keep every sample more than a meter from the next, in metal or ringglass, the only containers that hold it still. Study runs through recorded passages — temperature, pressure, distance, and signal tone logged while a tray rides the plume crossing.
descriptiveIdentity.risks: Within a meter of each other, thin films climb the ceramic toward the other sample; brought together, two samples spread into one moving sheet and sound a cluster of high-band tones loud enough on a signal sounder to bring the watch.

facts.function: Warm resonant condensate collected from the center of Ravel's outer nets
facts.availability: Held in six sealed trays from three plume passages

gmNotes.text: The moment players stow two trays in the same locker or carry them down a corridor together, the films climb the ceramic toward one another and the high-band tones start, loud enough on any signal sounder to bring whoever is on watch.

Only metal and ringglass hold the liquid in place, so in an ordinary galley or processing room it is already crossing the ceramic while the party improvises containment out of whatever the room happens to have.

entities.name: Ravel Water

entities.description: Ravel's Second Hull is a maintenance rumor about a second pressure shell that answers knocks from inside the inhabited hull.
entities.name: Ravel's Second Hull
entities.veilTagline: Ravel maintenance crews trade maps of a second pressure hull that answers every knock from inside the first.

entities.description: The Ravess Company is an armed treasure-taking crew watching Aldevra's entrances and following successful hunters into the treasury.

descriptiveIdentity.ideology: A valuable find belongs to the crew that can carry it away.
descriptiveIdentity.methods: Watch exits, follow fresh route marks and strike when a hunter's hands are full.
descriptiveIdentity.presence: Armed lodgers occupy rooms overlooking the bathing court and keep travel bags ready beside their doors.
descriptiveIdentity.attitude: Patient with another crew's exploration and brutal once the treasure is exposed.

gmNotes.text: A shutter opens above the bathing court as a laden hunter emerges. A second watcher leaves by the stair that reaches the street ahead of them.

entities.name: The Ravess Company

entities.description: The Red Sleeve is the signal-bearing arm of a faded pressure coat kept at Wash Four. Trace washers use its layered voice, engine rhythm, and route beacon to calibrate instruments and judge later textile records.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: One arm of a faded pressure coat, marked by tool abrasion, salt, and three repairs, kept at Wash Four. Its ringglass mordant holds three layers of signal apart along its length.
descriptiveIdentity.handling: Trace washers run portable paddles against it to calibrate: a good reading recovers a speaking voice at the cuff, an engine rhythm at the elbow, and a route beacon near the shoulder seam. Played in wash order, the voice's short phrases give directions through Wash Four's clean route.
descriptiveIdentity.risks: Each training wash weakens the quiet words first, so every calibration spends a little of the record. Because the sleeve fixes how fast a genuine trace should decay, garments measured against it more often fail than pass — including several whose voice is stronger than their treatment history permits.

facts.function: Provides a stable textile trace for field comparison and wash calibration

gmNotes.text: Every calibration a party asks for costs the sleeve something: the reading recovers the voice at the cuff, an engine rhythm at the elbow and a route beacon near the shoulder seam, and it strips the quiet words a little further each time.
The sleeve fixes how fast a genuine trace should decay, so measuring a promising find against it usually disqualifies the find rather than confirming it.

entities.name: The Red Sleeve

entities.description: The Red Sovereign is an Adversary mantle that extends Outside Will into standing commands over crews, vessels, armies, cities, and machine intelligences.

descriptiveIdentity.signs: The bearer's command sounds twice, a second red-toned voice answers inside each listener or machine, and subjects repeat the operative words before acting.
descriptiveIdentity.effect: The mantle extends EREFoutside_will|Outside Will||END from one immediate act to standing control of crews, vessels, armies, cities, and machine intelligences.
descriptiveIdentity.limits: A subject must receive, understand, and be capable of the order. The command supplies obedience rather than skill and follows the subject's literal meaning.

facts.qualification: Answers someone whose exact words are freely obeyed by a person who understands the order and can refuse it without punishment
facts.succession: Passes to a subject who knowingly disobeys an absolute command and reaches the bearer before punishment can fall
facts.cost: Resistance consumes the bearer's autobiographical memory; an absolute command destroys a memory equal in importance to what the subjects are made to betray

gmNotes.text: A direct command takes effect when the target receives it, understands its terms, and can perform the action; ambiguity resolves through the target's knowledge, while an impossible order fails without supplying a skill.
A subject who knowingly disobeys an absolute command and reaches the bearer becomes the possible successor, even while the same command continues through every person and machine that accepted it.

entities.name: The Red Sovereign

entities.description: Redband Nine is a marked cordon-scavenger colony that crosses the Bloom boundary between Pyre and Latch.
entities.name: Redband Nine
entities.veilTagline: Redband Nine crosses between Pyre and Latch whenever Bloom light reaches the red warning band.

entities.description: The Reed Clearing is a Lowbank ferry campaign against the dense growth choking Dovra's old channels.
entities.name: The Reed Clearing
entities.veilTagline: The Reed Clearing pits Lowbank ferry crews against the dense growth choking Dovra's old channels.

entities.description: The Reed Exchange is a trade network for kilnware, medicine, and living cuttings along Dovra's maintained channels.
entities.name: The Reed Exchange
entities.veilTagline: The Reed Exchange trades kilnware, medicines, and living cuttings along Dovra's maintained channels.

entities.description: The Reed Quarantine holds boats carrying red-root growth outside inhabited channels until every cutting remains silent.
entities.name: The Reed Quarantine
entities.veilTagline: The Reed Quarantine keeps boats carrying red-root growth outside inhabited channels until every cutting stays silent.

entities.description: Relay Colony Seven is a named signal-fed growth recorded at Span Nine, Issel, Far Bell, and Karet Three.
entities.name: Relay Colony Seven
entities.veilTagline: Relay Colony Seven grows the same shell pattern at Span Nine, Issel, Far Bell, and Karet Three in time with one repeated transmission.

entities.description: Renn Duvasi is a Pelhari archive scholar who joins damaged pre-Glassfall maintenance records to the casebooks of living Tuners.

descriptiveIdentity.disposition: Put a question about an old record to Duvasi and out come the damaged sheet, the copies taken from it, and the overlays where visiting mechanics disagreed, with an invitation to mark a new reading on the transparency.

facts.occupation: Archive scholar at the Pelhari academy
facts.specialty: Pre-Glassfall resonance maintenance records

gmNotes.text: Bring Duvasi readings that do not belong together — a dead heater, a distant refinery starting, a compass pointing into rock — and they map the set against known ringglass paths and say where the load went. The answer is good enough to choose the next survey site and is not a repair.

Duvasi answers a question about an old record by producing the damaged sheet, the copies taken from it, and the overlays where visiting mechanics disagreed. Whoever wanted one authoritative reading gets three and an invitation to mark their own on the transparency.

The second edition keeps Duvasi out of the archive and standing in the places their records describe, asking who rebuilt a wall and where a conduit went. Salvage crews meet them as a scholar with exact questions about a run of ringglass already sold.

entities.name: Renn Duvasi

entities.description: Renn Var is an archive-face cutter at Talven and the maker of Var's Wedge.

descriptiveIdentity.disposition: Offer to make the cut and Var hands over a damper or a listening point instead; she seats the wedge herself until an apprentice's readings have matched hers across three separate cuts.

facts.specialty: Separating recorded ringglass along the crystal grain

gmNotes.text: Offer to make the cut and Var hands over a damper or a listening point instead; she seats the wedge herself until an apprentice's readings have matched hers across three separate cuts.

[Echo Ledger Conclave](/glass-frontier/entry/echo-ledger-conclave) listeners work her bench and write down the cuts she refuses along with the signal lost in each one, so a bad call made in front of her is read elsewhere in the system.

entities.name: Renn Var

entities.description: The Repeated Voice is a 2435 recovery at Bay Thirty-One of one voice from twenty-seven unrelated garments.

descriptiveIdentity.marks: Twenty-seven garments and the ceramic maps made before washing sit at Thirty-One, arranged by the time of their last wash. Heard in that order, the voice gives directions through Wash Four's clean route, and the last garment calls a turn past the cylinder's sealed axial wall.
descriptiveIdentity.stakes: Certificates are suspended on the lots whose traces read stronger than their age permits, so their owners cannot sell the cloth on and are refusing the one destructive wash that would settle the question. Each further treatment removes the voice's quietest phrases.

gmNotes.text: The twenty-seven pieces came from surface caravans, ring tugs, a diplomatic courier and three local households with nothing in common, so any garment a party has had cleaned at [Wash Four](/glass-frontier/entry/wash-four) is a plausible twenty-eighth and gets pulled for mapping.
Players who ask to hear the whole thing are walked through it in wash order, and the last garment calls a turn past the cylinder's sealed axial wall that no clean-route lane reaches.
Certificates are suspended on the lots that read too strong, so their owners cannot sell the cloth on and are refusing the one destructive wash that would settle the question.

entities.name: The Repeated Voice

entities.description: Ressa Dorr is an Ithara provisioner who runs a crowded eating hall and equips small expeditions from her own stores.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: Broad hands with pale scald marks and close-cut gray hair.
descriptiveIdentity.attire: A dark apron over insulated trousers; a pressure hood hangs beside the serving hatch.
descriptiveIdentity.tools: Stacked food tins, a folding balance and keys worn on a short cloth loop.
descriptiveIdentity.manner: Finishes serving the person in front of her before answering the richest visitor in the room.
descriptiveIdentity.disposition: Wants independent crews solvent enough to remain customers; refuses to finance a voyage by starving the people waiting at home.

gmNotes.text: Over a meal, Ressa offers space in a provision load to Damarat if someone will bring Tamet's finished bowls back undented. A waiting crew wants the same spare space for a passenger.
Staying after the meal means helping clear a floor for the lodgers' bouts. Ressa hands a willing newcomer the patched sash and tells the regulars to show them the short-floor turn slowly.

entities.name: Ressa Dorr

entities.description: Ressa's grandmother died; Ressa inherited the eating hall, stores, outstanding debts and Sereyat.
entities.name: Ressa Inherits Hall

entities.description: Reth is a hand-raised eshkul moving between Iridess and Naloven, familiar with the battery's orchard lift and dangerous when its handlers use it to obstruct patrols.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: A broad-backed adult with a pale ring around its tail and a bare crescent above one shoulder where old burns destroyed the spines.
descriptiveIdentity.behavior: Answers three slow taps, sleeps above an orchard lift and carries favored fruit away before eating it.
descriptiveIdentity.threat: Can block a narrow crossing with a resin display, then flee toward familiar people if frightened by a shot.

gmNotes.text: Three slow taps draw Reth down toward a familiar feeder. A shot can send it climbing toward that person, scattering resin over companions who expected the animal to keep the pursuers away.

entities.name: Reth

entities.description: The Returning Casing is one of three original stillwater buoy casings mounted at Cinder Gap; it returns a faint copy of every test tone applied nearby.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: One of three original buoy casings mounted behind Cinder Gap's current wall.
descriptiveIdentity.handling: Work begins with remote taps and isolated samples; Lira Vashtenri prohibits opening it until a crew can show where its stored frequencies will go.
descriptiveIdentity.risks: Its stillwater has absorbed decades of cascade activity, and the casing returns a faint version of every test tone applied near it.

gmNotes.text: Instrument work anywhere near the old mounts picks up a second voice, because the Returning Casing gives back a faint version of every test tone applied to it. Crews new to the section read that as a fault in their own equipment and lose an hour chasing it.
Proposing to open the saturated casing gets a condition rather than a refusal: Lira Vashtenri requires the crew to show where the stored frequencies will go once the vessel is breached.

entities.name: The Returning Casing

entities.description: The Returning Pods are six cargo pods that arrived at Clearance Eight in 2435 carrying recently lost household objects repaired and resealed.

descriptiveIdentity.marks: Six pods sit in one powered custody row at Clearance Eight, an Eighth Seal fixed inside every lid with current impressions from all eight desks in their proper order. Tangent works the approach line beyond the cleared lane, carrying an empty cradle and a reader loaded with the six seal sequences.
descriptiveIdentity.stakes: The ownership desk could return each object today; the identity and route desks refuse to close the cases while the fresh seals remain unexplained. Every day in custody adds storage debt against claimants who never asked for the repair or chose the return route.

gmNotes.text: The six claimants live at [Clearance Eight](/glass-frontier/entry/clearance-eight) and lost the objects on separate recent journeys, so any character who has misplaced gear on a run can be called into a claim room to identify a repaired version of it.

Every day the identity and route desks hold the cases open adds storage debt to claimants who never asked for the repair, so the people pressing hardest for a disposition are residents watching a bill grow against something they already own.

entities.name: The Returning Pods

entities.description: Rib is a small settlement inside a living pressure reef in the Glass Frontier, built along one exposed ring support and maintained through the reef's pulse.

descriptiveIdentity.setting: Narrow terraces cut between old alloy and living stone inside a growing pressure reef, curved around the one exposed ring support at the center. Room walls breathe through soft filter mouths, and the reef's low structural pulses travel up through floors, pipes, and the hard belly plates of grazing sorel.
descriptiveIdentity.activity: The pulse is the schedule: cutters open passages during the long low note while new mineral is soft, filter crews climb during the short rising pattern that drives grit outward, and meals gather on the terraces in the quiet interval while the reef moves its water.
descriptiveIdentity.access: Filter carriers from Vey and timber loads from Noll come in through the single approach trench kept open in the outer shell.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: Dust, spores, smoke, or cutting work makes a room's filter mouths contract, and its air supply stops until they reopen. The fourth terrace is closing a handspan at a time, fresh shell creeping over doors, rail sockets, and three generations of painted measure marks.

facts.population_band: About four hundred and sixty residents
facts.role: Cultivation of a living pressure shell and biological air filters
facts.setting: Terraces built along one exposed ring support inside a growing reef
facts.access: Filter carriers from Vey and timber loads from Noll through one approach trench kept open in the outer shell

gmNotes.text: Rib's day runs on the reef's pulse rather than any clock. Cutters will open a passage only during the long low note, filter crews climb during the short rising pattern, and a party wanting either job done waits for the interval that suits it.

Dust, spores, smoke, or cutting work inside a room makes the filter mouths in its walls contract, and the room's air supply stops until they open again. Any fight or hurried repair indoors becomes a question of how long that room holds.

There is one carrier's worth of space to argue over while the fourth terrace closes a handspan at a time: the filter crews want the sealed reef bud carried to [Vey](/glass-frontier/entry/vey), and the households beside the narrowing doors want that space for children, tools, and stored food.

entities.name: Rib

entities.description: The Rib Sorel Herds are the grazing animals bred and marked by Rib households to expose growth and load paths in the settlement's pressure reef. Cutters use their movement before opening new chambers.

gmNotes.text: A cutter brings one marked herd into a new chamber before opening it, then reads cropped growth, untouched ridges, and where the animals settle.
When the reef's note shifts, the whole herd crosses to the next tone line together, carrying anything standing across it into the wall.
Away from Rib's reef, each animal needs a living shell pad and tuned brace; a failed pad swings the transport cradle toward the strongest structural tone aboard.

entities.name: The Rib Sorel Herds

entities.description: The Ring Collective is the standing assembly through which connected ring habitats present common positions without surrendering local law.

descriptiveIdentity.ideology: Connected habs should speak together without surrendering an ounce of local law: any member may reject a resolution, and membership belongs to the habitat itself, not to whoever governs it. The assembly refuses to judge whether a Session's instructions or a civic appointment is the more legitimate way to send a delegation.
descriptiveIdentity.methods: Sovereignty and contact questions get one voice per hab; freight and maintenance measures weigh declared population and traffic, so a port carries more when it accepts more work. Most resolutions pair a common minimum with voluntary agreements among members who need more, and the standing work is registry: who accepts contact, which seals are compatible, what routes are closed.
descriptiveIdentity.presence: Delegation rooms and the route register at Hab Meridian, staffed largely with relay time and clerks the big ports provide — a dependence the smaller members resent in a nominally equal assembly. Each delegation arrives under whatever process its own hab recognizes.
descriptiveIdentity.attitude: To anyone approaching a ring hab, it is the register consulted first: contact terms, quarantine notices, closures. To those who want it to compel a member, it offers a resolution at most — it claims no right to open a hatch, inspect an interior, or seat a delegation outsiders have sent, though it will relay a message to a shuttered hab where a recognized channel exists.

facts.mandate: Represent connected ring habitats in shared route, salvage, and sovereignty matters

gmNotes.text: An approach to any ring hab is checked against the Collective's register, which records who accepts contact, who requires terms agreed in advance, and who has withdrawn, alongside compatible docking seals, quarantine notices, and current route closures.

Asking the Collective to make a member do something produces a resolution at most. Each hab keeps its own law and may reject one, and the assembly claims no right to open a hatch, inspect an interior, or seat a delegation outsiders have sent.

A damaged vessel looking for a berth lands in the assembly's open dispute: large ports want authority to redirect it to any member with a compatible seal, small habs require the receiving hab's consent first, and the route notice waits on that argument.

entities.name: Ring Collective

entities.description: Rings-Twice is an itinerant storyteller and parts trader working between Wash Four and Carom.
entities.name: Rings-Twice
entities.veilTagline: Rings-Twice trades stories for spare parts and repeats each story differently at Wash Four and Carom.

entities.description: The Room Before the Ice is a furnished Ring Age apartment melting free of Mera's Fourth Column, with the thawglass frame passing through its walls as though the room predated the column.

descriptiveIdentity.setting: A complete Ring Age apartment inside Mera's Fourth Column, furnished with Ring Age chairs and a sealed interior door.
descriptiveIdentity.activity: Ward readers post the falling water level beside two competing claims while the bright-season market occupies the surrounding stairs.
descriptiveIdentity.access: The apartment opens as the Fourth Column melts free around it; Mera has diverted the next spill channel away from the room.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: The thawglass frame passes through its walls, and the diversion sends one water ward's garden share through another ward's public column.

gmNotes.text: The apartment opens a little farther each day as the Fourth Column melts, while ward readers post the falling water level beside each claim.
Two water wards have filed against each other: one for the lost spring flow, the other for the room now occupying its frame.

entities.name: The Room Before the Ice

entities.description: The Root Commons is a mutual-aid network that moves food and air workers among Noll, Rib, Vey, and Lung Three.
entities.name: The Root Commons
entities.veilTagline: The Root Commons moves food and air workers among four habs whenever one garden loses heat.

entities.description: The Root Door Engine is a passage-opening machine used in the Underlayers, Folded Annex, and Old Campus. It borrows structural tension from an adjoining wall to open sealed ring doors.
entities.name: Root Door Engine
entities.veilTagline: The Root Door Engine opens sealed ring passages by borrowing structural tension from the adjoining wall.

entities.description: Root Exchange is a graft-trading network among households in Mera, Noll, Orra, and Olven that transfers living plants without pricing them as coin.
entities.name: Root Exchange
entities.veilTagline: Root Exchange households trade living grafts among Mera, Noll, Orra, and Olven without converting them into coin.

entities.description: The Rootward Migration moved Noll gardeners and their soil beds into Olven after a root deck cooled beyond recovery.
entities.name: The Rootward Migration
entities.veilTagline: Noll gardeners moved into Olven with their soil beds after a whole root deck cooled beyond recovery.

entities.description: Ruvian is a working vessel restored in 2429, carrying its former restorer beside the missing bow gallery she left unrecovered.

gmNotes.text: Walking Ruvian with someone preparing a restoration brings the visitors to its absent gallery, where the crew explains both the working's preserved loss and the useful changes made afterward.

entities.name: Ruvian

entities.description: The previous Great Restorer returned Ruvian, preserved the absent gallery, lost depth perception and disclosed the working before Eris received the mantle.
entities.name: Ruvian Restored

entities.description: The return of Ruvian in 2429 restored a working vessel and passed the Great Restorer to Eris Talven after its previous bearer disclosed the preserved loss.

gmNotes.text: Someone preparing a restoration seeks out Ruvian's crew to learn what the returned flaws and chosen omission meant after the restorer left.

entities.name: The Return of Ruvian

entities.description: The Sable Crescent is a warm river basin on Kaleidos whose marshes, cliffs, and canyons contain the system's densest concentration of Echo Rivers.

descriptiveIdentity.setting: A warm river basin hooked around an ancient impact floor, marsh and flooded plain at its center, high cliffs and deep canyons cutting the rim where crystal-bearing strata glow faintly after sunset. Water moving through the laced sediment comes back to the surface carrying voices, and at dusk the exposed strata refract low sun through the marsh mist into pale bands the residents call glasslight.
descriptiveIdentity.activity: Shallow broad-bottomed boats carry most freight below the cliffs, piloted by ear as much as eye, while farms work raised beds in the delta soil and crews wash low-grade ringglass out of the sediment traps after floods. Ledgerfall holds the big market, Thornvault anchors the Echo Ledger Conclave's listening work, and journeys are planned by water level and gate schedule as much as by distance.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: A channel with a strong new signal may hide a fresh deposit or an undercut bank, and an uncovered lamp in glasslight repeats through several banks until another boat reads far closer than it is. An upstream council holding water to save its own crop sends a sharper rise into the next district, so the flood arrives carrying somebody's decision.

facts.present_here: Disappearance of the Elves, The Glassfall, The Open Roads, The Thornvault Echo Guide, The Verathi Quiet, Thornvault Backecho

gmNotes.text: Distance here is water level and gate schedule rather than ground. A rim town can stand directly above a stilt village and still cost a full day of stairs, ferries and narrow lifts to reach.

Travel at dusk brings glasslight, and an uncovered lamp repeats through several banks of exposed strata until another boat reads as much closer than it is. Crescent crews run shaded lamps until the bands fade.

Gate schedules are negotiated across the whole basin before the wet season, so an upstream council holding water to save its own crop sends a sharper rise downstream. Anyone the party is bargaining with below is already watching the highland gauges.

entities.name: Sable Crescent

entities.description: Sable Korr failed Fermata's citizenship Sit-In in 2405 after following a written Standard more closely than the other musicians.
entities.name: Sable Failed Sit In

entities.description: Sable Korr is the keeper of Fermata Station's informal Session archive and an Audience member excluded from formal performance.

descriptiveIdentity.disposition: Sable answers in full sentences, sets the conflicting accounts side by side, and does not recommend a choice. A buyer who wants a recording without its dispute does not get the sale.

facts.occupation: Standard scholar and keeper of Fermata's Session archive

gmNotes.text: Ask Sable what an earlier Session meant and she supplies the recording, the witness account that contradicts it, and the repair report showing the room's pulse slowed on its own. She names the conflict without recommending a reading, so the choice gets made in front of the hall.

Her failed Sit-In bars Sable from voting, calling a tune, or playing a governing solo, so nothing she knows can enter a Session in her own voice. Her evidence needs a citizen willing to play it and to carry whatever it does to the argument.

Copies of Fermata's Session recordings sell to visiting scholars during [the Fermata Open](/glass-frontier/entry/the-fermata-open), and Sable sends each one out with the dispute, the repair report, and the witness accounts attached. A buyer who wants the performance alone does not get the sale.

entities.name: Sable Korr

entities.description: Sahel is the conventional name of an ancient Itharan builder witnessed restoring homes and later destroying the recoverability of a defense during an evacuation.

facts.specialty: Distributed pattern keeping and the deliberate breaking of recoverability

gmNotes.text: A piece associated with Sahel fits a damaged work perfectly except where a deliberate cut prevents the return; a collector offers an alternative witness from another site.

entities.name: Sahel

entities.description: Sahel's Breach is an ancient Itharan evacuation in which deliberate destruction of surviving patterns kept a broken fortification from returning across the departing people's route.

gmNotes.text: Searching for a missing defensive component reveals deliberate destruction and a departure trail; following the trail may recover an alternative witness or explain one household's escape.

entities.name: Sahel's Breach

entities.description: Sava Neraleth was the Istravan League's founder, who joined the coastal cities' defenses and returned wartime authority to them after the Bitter Reach.

gmNotes.text: A harbor asked to shelter strangers produces one of Sava's commitments naming that household's old service; another resident produces the order that removed the town's defenders.

entities.name: Sava Neraleth

entities.description: Sava Neraleth died, leaving the league's member councils to choose a commander without her personal authority.
entities.name: Sava Neraleth Died

entities.description: Savren is Velisar's captured cliff battery, with seaward guns, an inland command hall and prisoner rooms inside its old protected galleries.

descriptiveIdentity.setting: Gun terraces project from a black cliff while a tiled command hall faces the city's gardens.
descriptiveIdentity.activity: Crews turn the seaward mounts, families wait at the upper gate and prisoners mend equipment behind the inner shutters.
descriptiveIdentity.access: The inland gate takes vehicles; cable galleries connect the terraces and a sea stair reaches an old boat recess.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: Each gun leaves a different blind angle; live receivers carry the sovereign's voice, and compelled defenders may fight beside willing comrades.

facts.function: Defends the harbor mouth and provides a protected command position above the city

gmNotes.text: A family waits at the battery gate with food and a child's drawing. The guard recognizes the visitor and quietly indicates a different stair.
A gunner will open a service hatch if her whole crew comes out. One of them still obeys an order to hold the mount and begins fastening himself to its frame.

entities.name: Savren

entities.description: Seamkeeper is a named Ravel clampweed growth traced through hull seams at Ravel and Tanel.
entities.name: Seamkeeper
entities.veilTagline: Seamkeeper runs through the hull seams of Ravel and Tanel and grips both during the same signal tides.

entities.description: Second Channel is the migrating route avulsion tracked on the Keel: after two fixed warning tones, a busy corridor begins delivering all traffic to a destination impressed into it by earlier journeys.

descriptiveIdentity.signs: Every beacon and hull on a busy corridor sounds one hull-deep tone and, after the same measured interval, one high tone while the forward view remains unchanged.
descriptiveIdentity.effects: Traffic still on the marked line after the second tone reaches the destination most strongly preserved in the corridor's wakes and return vectors.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: Whole convoys arrive without reception, and rescue craft that follow the old line travel to the same new terminus instead of the port that called them.

facts.trigger: Repeated transit makes a corridor's combined kinetic and signal wake more coherent than its maintained approach to the published terminus
facts.effect: After the second warning tone, every vessel remaining on the corridor reaches the strongest destination encoded in its accumulated journeys
facts.recurrence: One avulsion migrates among the system's busiest routes, preserving the exact interval between its low first tone and high second tone
facts.ending: The chosen terminus persists until another path accumulates the stronger coherent wake; the abandoned destination remains reachable only by different geometry
facts.mitigation: Leave the marked corridor after the first tone, rebuild the abandoned approach from an independent bearing, or saturate a prepared diversion before the second tone
facts.anchor_behavior: Follows accumulated transit rather than route ownership or beacon placement, carrying its warning interval into the next busy corridor
facts.medium: Established corridors, vessel wakes, route beacons, joined route records, and repeated destination approaches
facts.content: The accumulated return vectors, diversions, refuges, and ambush approaches carried by traffic through the active corridor
facts.hazard: Convoys, rescue craft, refugees, and cargo can arrive together at an unprepared or hostile destination while the port expecting them loses that approach

gmNotes.text: The low and high warning tones sound across a convoy at their fixed interval, leaving every vessel on the marked line time to break away or add its wake to the destination the corridor is choosing.

entities.name: Second Channel

entities.description: The Second Span Trial was Coremark's failed 2356 attempt to build a modern counterpart to Span Nine through the mid-drift.

descriptiveIdentity.marks: A chain of aligned ringglass anchor beds still sits through the mid-drift, stripped of transmitters and cut crystal, each segment testing inert on its own — the same test that once signed the chain off as a passive guide. The complete project records, down to the rejected readings of Pyre answering a silent array, rest with the Shear Compact.
descriptiveIdentity.stakes: Sithari keeps the only working span and no replacement has been attempted since, so the inequality that financed the trial has no outlet. The aligned mass in the beds is an obvious payday, and certification to strip it runs through the Compact that holds the record of what the chain carried.

gmNotes.text: The anchor beds are still seated through the mid-drift, stripped of transmitters and cut crystal and still heavy with aligned ringglass, and each one tests inert when tested alone. That is exactly the test the project crews ran before signing the chain off as a passive guide.

Stripping a bed for its aligned ringglass is the obvious payday, since Coremark left the mass only because hauling it cost more than it was worth. Certification for that work runs through the [Shear Compact](/glass-frontier/entry/shear-compact), which holds Voss's records of what the chain carried.

Sithari still holds the only working span and no replacement has been attempted since the trial closed, so the grievance that financed it has no outlet. Raising a second span in political company gets the Bloom's route through the abandoned anchors read back at the proposer.

entities.name: Second Span Trial

entities.description: The Seed-Share Order requires half of every revived Orra strain to reach a second habitat before local planting begins.
entities.name: The Seed-Share Order
entities.veilTagline: The Seed-Share Order sends half of every revived Orra strain to a second habitat before local planting begins.

entities.description: Selk is a small orchard hab whose pool shrine offers journeys through the senses of animals living beneath its settled decks.

descriptiveIdentity.setting: Orchard walks cover vaulted lower decks; a shrine pool lies beside low couches worn smooth at the water's edge.
descriptiveIdentity.activity: Pilgrims speak their borrowed sensations aloud while companions compare them with surface measurements.
descriptiveIdentity.access: Garden traffic links the hab with Seren; the pool opens directly from the orchard walk.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: A frightened animal may retreat into water too narrow for a person, carrying a pilgrim's awareness with it.

gmNotes.text: A pilgrim describing the orchard as branching pulses can abruptly fall silent when the animal turns toward a dense moving presence beneath the roots. Their surface companion still sees an empty path.

entities.name: Selk

entities.description: The Selk Swimmers are the enuli living between the shrine pool and the hab's lower waters, carrying sensations and small objects between them.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: Pale blind swimmers bear occasional soft bands holding ornaments or sealed messages.
descriptiveIdentity.behavior: Return to the warm shrine pool after feeding through different lower passages.
descriptiveIdentity.threat: A frightened swimmer abandons a familiar route and can take a message into unsurveyed water.

gmNotes.text: A swimmer surfaces with a differently tied band. Its keeper recognizes the animal's scar, but the knot and the object inside it came from elsewhere.

entities.name: The Selk Swimmers

entities.description: Selven Iral finances extended Lithren expeditions and seeks a restored Itharan stronghold whose recovered military works he can control.

gmNotes.text: Asking Selven for a fragment needed by a return brings an offer of access tied to who will control the recovered defense; workers who owe him a rescue argue his case.

entities.name: Selven Iral

entities.description: Sen'ket is the passive-array mechanic who maintains Issel's longest surviving receiver baseline.

descriptiveIdentity.disposition: Sen'ket keeps a section comparison running while talking, so replies arrive at the cart's pace and out of order. A question about a past failure opens the numbered drawers beneath the array.

facts.specialty: Timing long receiver baselines through damaged ringglass

gmNotes.text: Sen'ket is somewhere along the baseline with the hand cart and the shielded clock, and keeps a section comparison running while talking. Breaking the run costs that section's timing, so answers come at the cart's pace and out of order.

Ask when a stretch of the array last failed and Sen'ket opens the numbered drawers beneath it, where every removed cable fragment is kept in order. The fragments date the repair and still hold the signal response of the run they were cut from.

Sen'ket's first three listening beads took the [Long Note](/glass-frontier/entry/long-note) before their cables reached the dish, so they will not accept a disconnected instrument as proof that nothing was heard. Any test a party proposes gains a disconnected control bead before Sen'ket will argue from its result.

entities.name: Sen'ket

entities.description: Senn Ravel is a freight-record dissident who posts erased claims on public walls at Ravel and Third Latch.
entities.name: Senn Ravel
entities.veilTagline: Senn Ravel posts erased freight claims on the public walls of Ravel and Third Latch.

entities.description: Senra Veth is a Kyrri ground-reader who works between Vigil Breach, the Kyther Range, Avar, and Ladderwell.
entities.name: Senra Veth
entities.veilTagline: Senra Veth keeps a scored plate of every ground-tone change measured between Vigil Breach, the Kyther Range, Avar, and Ladderwell.

entities.description: Seren is a biological repository settlement in the Glass Frontier, occupying a cold Ring-era spindle divided between sealed vaults and warm trial beds.

descriptiveIdentity.setting: A cold Ring-era spindle turning slowly through its own shadow: numbered vaults behind ceramic corridors on the dark half, stepped gardens, humid growth rooms, and shallow tanks on the sunward half, with air and tools moving from clean rooms toward trial beds along painted one-way routes.
descriptiveIdentity.activity: Visiting crews prove their cultures can live outside storage, tending the first growth themselves in trial beds matched to the declared source while Seren workers record every intervention. A deposit that survives earns a vault number and enters exchange, paid in stock rather than coin.
descriptiveIdentity.access: The clean-stock circuit from Orra and Olven serves one freight lock and two passenger locks on the shaded end.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: Walking a painted corridor backwards contaminates everything between you and the vaults, and residents will say so before you reach the far door. A viable stock with a poor cultivation account is the deeper danger — it can drink a habitat's water or crowd out its food plants before the error shows.

facts.population_band: About eighteen hundred residents, with several hundred seasonal depositors
facts.role: Custody, propagation, and exchange of biological stocks
facts.setting: A cold Ring-era spindle divided between sealed vaults and warm trial beds
facts.access: Clean-stock circuit from Orra and Olven to one freight lock and two passenger locks on the shaded end

gmNotes.text: A crew carrying anything alive can deposit it here, but a deposit is three parts and the third is a written account of growing it. Depositors tend the first growth themselves, which keeps a party on the spindle for a season instead of an afternoon.

Seren pays in stock rather than coin. A deposit that survives its trial bed draws equivalent cultures from the public catalog or shares of later propagation, which is how a party with no money leaves with medicine.

Air, tools, and people move one way here, from the clean rooms toward the trial beds along painted routes. Walking a painted corridor backwards contaminates everything between you and the vaults, and the residents will say so before you reach the far door.

entities.name: Seren

entities.description: Sereva is an association of Ashvane highland towns sending a military and rescue expedition to Istrava, where many of its households have relatives.

gmNotes.text: A Serevan crew assigned to hold a captured position learns that its home town needs its mechanics back; Hareth needs a replacement before he will extend the deployment.

entities.name: Sereva

entities.description: Serevan households received the people carried from Velisar's eastern quays.
entities.name: Sereva Receives Evacuees

entities.description: Sereyat is an ancient Lithren percussion instrument kept in Ressa Dorr's Ithara hall, whose sale and performances helped finance the early settlement.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: Hollow curved ceramic ribs rise from a low metal frame; sliding shoes beneath them change the length left free to vibrate.
descriptiveIdentity.handling: Players strike or rub the ribs from opposite sides. A lowered crossbar puts one bank within a seated player's reach.
descriptiveIdentity.risks: Cold ribs crack under hard blows; gripping a sounding surface damps its note. Moving the frame without its braces strains old repairs.

facts.function: Sounds ceramic ribs whose pitch changes with the position of their support shoes

gmNotes.text: A visiting musician offers passage and a share of performance receipts for help carrying Sereyat inward. Ressa wants enough to advance her garden, while regular listeners begin gathering money to keep the instrument in Ithara.
Humming along draws an answering phrase from the other bank. After the paid performance, a player offers to show the visitor where their remembered version parts from the hall's.

entities.name: Sereyat

entities.description: Nereth's comparisons established the ancient use and retention of Sereyat's lowered playing bank.
entities.name: Sereyat Adaptation Witnessed

entities.description: The returning percussionists brought Sereyat arrangements to Istrava and played them on a modern portable rib frame.
entities.name: Sereyat Arrangements Reach Veyr

entities.description: Ressa's grandmother bought Sereyat back for performances in the settlement's eating hall.
entities.name: Sereyat Brought Home

entities.description: Pelhari performances drew further buyers and expeditions seeking working Lithren finds.
entities.name: Sereyat Performed Pelhari

entities.description: An excavating crew recovered Sereyat and sold it on Pelhari, financing rooms and another voyage.
entities.name: Sereyat Recovered And Sold

entities.description: The Seven-New Load is sealed cargo aboard Nine Holds at Keelward, entered as Korvathi insulating tile but answering the ship's sounder as instrument-grade ringglass on alternating tests.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: A sealed cargo in the replacement seventh hold of Nine Holds, covered by a valid Korvathi ceramic manifest.
descriptiveIdentity.working: The ship's sounder records insulating tile and instrument-grade ringglass responses in alternating tests; Keelward will not release it into a warehouse and the insurer will not cover an exterior opening.
descriptiveIdentity.risks: The consignee refuses the ringglass duty while the partners charge for a voyage the ship cannot finish with the cargo still attached.

gmNotes.text: The sealed load alternates between insulating-tile and instrument-grade ringglass responses under the ship's own sounder.
Opening it outside is excluded by the insurer, while Keelward refuses to release the box into a warehouse.
The consignee holds a valid ceramic manifest and refuses the ringglass duty while Nine Holds charges for every day the cargo keeps the ship at berth.

entities.name: The Seven-New Load

entities.description: The Seven-Tine Gauge is a salvage-testing instrument used between Pell Cut and Crowncut Refinery. It identifies material that can be refined without releasing its trapped kinetic charge.
entities.name: The Seven-Tine Gauge
entities.veilTagline: The Seven-Tine Gauge identifies salvage that Crowncut can refine without waking its trapped kinetic charge.

entities.description: The Severance is an Istravan resistance group trying to end Aren's rule while keeping prospective successors from taking the Red Sovereign.

descriptiveIdentity.ideology: Free the coast and prevent another bearer from acquiring the power to command it.
descriptiveIdentity.methods: Hide prospective claimants, interrupt escorts, cut live command channels and sabotage weapons sought by Aren's forces.
descriptiveIdentity.presence: Small parties with unrelated trades, meeting among singers, quarry workers and displaced households.
descriptiveIdentity.attitude: Accepts cooperation for a rescue while arguing openly against any plan to crown its beneficiary.

gmNotes.text: A person the visitors agreed to escort has taken the Severance's offer of passage away. Their companion says the decision was freely made; another member admits withholding letters from the waiting rescuers.

entities.name: The Severance

entities.description: Sevrin is the grounded carrier at Ithara whose 2311 landfall and conversion to occupied rooms in 2322 established a lasting foothold on Lithren.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: A broad worn hull rests in a stone cradle, with covered passages leaving its former cargo hatches and blank plates over the flight fittings.
descriptiveIdentity.aboard: Low sleeping compartments open around a former hold; an old exterior window faces a passage now enclosed by a later pressure hall.
descriptiveIdentity.behavior: The ship remains occupied and connected to modern heat and air. It cannot fly in its present condition.

gmNotes.text: The room offered for a visit contains an early specimen box used as a table. Its owner will explain who brought it home, but expects any examination to happen while the household continues eating and working.

entities.name: Sevrin

entities.description: Residents and visiting crews defeated Sevrin's armed eviction; the households retained their rooms under different owners.
entities.name: Sevrin Eviction Defeated

entities.description: Collector earnings paid for separate sleeping rooms and a covered connection to new ground-level housing.
entities.name: Sevrin Partitioned

entities.description: The Sevrin Pledge is a shelter rule upheld by Ithara households and carriers: a person facing exposure may enter a participating refuge after surrendering weapons, even while wanted by its occupants.

gmNotes.text: A disarmed robber reaches a pledged shelter whose occupants include someone they injured. The pursuer demands immediate surrender; the guest offers the location of surviving captives if allowed to remain alive and under guard.

entities.name: The Sevrin Pledge

entities.description: Sevrin households and visiting carriers undertook to shelter disarmed people facing exposure after the fighting.
entities.name: Sevrin Pledge Stated

entities.description: Vedra grounded Sevrin permanently and converted its compartments into continuously occupied shelter.
entities.name: Sevrin Settled

entities.description: The Sevrin Stand was the defeat of an armed attempt to evict households from Ithara's grounded carrier in 2372.

gmNotes.text: An attempt to clear occupied rooms brings neighbors through Sevrin's service passage with supplies and weapons. Some defend tenants they dislike; they want the rooms left occupied, not a new leader for the settlement.

entities.name: The Sevrin Stand

entities.description: The Shade Condensing Frame is a water machine used around Shadewell, South Shade, and Coldside Bench. It draws clean water from Ashvane pressure exhaust and cracks when the wind reverses.
entities.name: Shade Condensing Frame
entities.veilTagline: The Shade Condensing Frame pulls clean water from Ashvane's pressure exhaust and cracks when the wind reverses.

entities.description: Shadewell is Ashvane's main port city, terraced down a shaded crater wall above the moon's largest accessible ice lens.

descriptiveIdentity.setting: A city terraced down the shaded inner wall of a deep crater on Ashvane, with reservoirs and cold stores in the lower rock above a buried ice lens and the freight port out on the sunward rim. Inclined rail, cargo lifts, and a covered stair road join the two halves, and the stair crosses from direct heat into the first cool terrace like a doorway.
descriptiveIdentity.activity: Cargo waits under reflective sheds on the rim until its temperature and field equalize, while below, water moves stage by stage from drinking storage through clinics, workshops, and washing to the terrace fields. Public courts where return lines meet stay warm after sunset and fill with food stalls, repair tables, and evening meetings.
descriptiveIdentity.access: The Keel terminus on the rim takes heavy kites onto basalt pads, with regional kites, heat-road haulers, and crater lifts carrying traffic onward. Porters in the passenger halls check a visitor's outer layers before pointing them at a surface exit.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: A crate that came down cold enough to contract can break its restraints halfway down the crater wall, and a person dressed for the crater can be hurt crossing one unshaded freight apron. Tapping a public return line out of registered order leaves the next use downhill cold, and the city finds the tap by temperature.

facts.population_band: About two hundred forty thousand across the crater city and port ridge
facts.role: Largest city on Ashvane and surface terminus of the Keel
facts.setting: Terraced crater wall above a deep ice lens, beside a high freight ridge
facts.access: Keel port, regional kites, heat-road haulers, and crater lifts

gmNotes.text: Freight off the Keel sits under the reflective sheds until its temperature and field equalize, so a shipment can be on Ashvane for a full day and still not be in the city. A crate that came down cold enough to contract can break its restraints halfway down the crater wall.

Attaching a kiln, pump, or heater to a public return line takes a registered place in the chain; done without notice it leaves the next use downhill cold and overheats the line beyond it. The city finds such taps by temperature, and a warm stair wall locates one before anyone admits to it.

Two lower return lines are shut while crews drill a new temperature shaft, so port repair yards run short shifts through the hot hours and workshop jobs queue with no promised date. Rim businesses want them open before the next heavy Keel arrivals and will push visitors to argue it to the terrace wards.

entities.name: Shadewell

entities.description: The Shadewell Pressure Herd feeds on hot mineral film outside Shadewell and nearby Ashvane settlements. Before storms, it runs toward sealed workshops.
entities.name: The Shadewell Pressure Herd
entities.veilTagline: The Shadewell Pressure Herd crops the hot mineral film outside the settlement and stampedes toward sealed workshops before storms.

entities.description: Shardfall was a four-day salvage battle and resonance cascade beside Brake in 2348 that killed forty-seven people.

descriptiveIdentity.marks: Forty-seven cut marks run along the replacement rail of Brake's observation gallery, two dead Drossmark frames hold sorting work in the cutting yards, and permanent rescue stores wait at the capture lanes, paid for by the field's last load. 'Another Shardfall' names any salvage risk that crosses into someone else's air, route, or structure.
descriptiveIdentity.stakes: An operator who claims a private salvage risk ends at the edge of their own vessel gets Brake's recordings quoted back, and Compact inspectors reach for the event whenever a linked field is treated as separate machines. Brake settles claim hearings from drive sequences because this one fixed who moved, who fired, and which arrays stayed active.

facts.participants: Brake, Brake Free Cutters, Drossmark Industries, Split Wake
facts.cause_status: Drossmark continued linked extraction after Brake's arrestors began answering the rigs

gmNotes.text: "Another Shardfall" is what people call a salvage risk that has crossed into someone else's air, route or structure, and Compact inspectors say it to an operator who is treating a linked field as separate machines.

Fixing several debris masses and a carrier into one cutting field is the arrangement that answered Brake's arrestors, and a hab with kinetic arrays orders the work stopped as soon as its instruments begin echoing the extraction tone.

[Brake](/glass-frontier/entry/brake) settles claim hearings from drive sequences because this one fixed who moved, who fired and which arrays stayed active, so a party arguing a claim there is arguing against its own logs.

entities.name: Shardfall

entities.description: Shared Gravity is a four-hab counterweight system that coordinates local force schedules so freight arrives under the gravity for which it was packed.
entities.name: Shared Gravity
entities.veilTagline: Shared Gravity links four habs that trade counterweight schedules so cargo arrives under the force it was packed for.

entities.description: The Shared Reference is a master three-reed tuning compass used to calibrate Counterweight and Underlayers field instruments. Its fixed tones descend from the Open Reed and remain the comparison carried into road-rig and deep-route work.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: Three long paired reeds around a clear ringglass bead in a rotating case, with Counterweight lift marks on one rim and Underlayers route marks on the other.
descriptiveIdentity.handling: Field compasses are placed beside the master case and turned through each band. A free reed that fails to reproduce its beat is repaired before the instrument returns to work.
descriptiveIdentity.risks: The reference reads gradients rather than causes and can itself bend under a strong narrow-band effect. Every calibration stops when its reeds and a Tuner's bodily reading disagree.

facts.function: Provides the fixed three-band reference used to calibrate field tuning compasses

gmNotes.text: The Shared Reference is called in when two working compasses disagree and neither crew will accept the other's calibration marks.
A Tuner who disagrees with the master reading stops the comparison; fatigue can distort the person and a bent reed can distort the instrument.
Moving the master compass from a Counterweight lift to an Underlayers closure leaves one crew working from its last accepted calibration.

entities.name: The Shared Reference

entities.description: The Shear Compact is the standards and mediation body that certifies salvage operators and regulates extraction in the Shear.

descriptiveIdentity.ideology: Nothing that happened at Pyre gets to happen again: minimum standards, extraction limits, and mediated claims are worth more than any single haul. Its authority rests on that memory rather than on force — the Compact keeps no armed arm at all.
descriptiveIdentity.methods: Certification by equipment inspection, crew competency assessment, and compliance with extraction limits; a Shear weather service tracking debris, resonance tides, and drift events; mediation of salvage disputes before anything reaches the Tempered Accord; and fines sized to deter casual corner-cutting, which determined violators simply pay as a cost of business.
descriptiveIdentity.presence: Survey crews sound working routes, inspectors test filters and cutters, and mediators hear competing accounts of a find. The forecast turns local sightings into warnings that other crews can compare with the opening ahead of them.
descriptiveIdentity.attitude: It wants independent operators inside shared safety and claim standards. A crew outside them can still launch, but loses Compact help in defending a find and faces fines at ports that enforce its decisions.

gmNotes.text: A fresh sighting contradicts the charted clearance ahead. The Compact asks nearby vessels for their returns while captains decide whether the remaining opening is wide enough for the loaded ship behind them.

A weaker crew can bring its recovery marks and witnesses to the Compact after a rival takes possession of a find. A receiving yard that honors the settlement can hold the sale open while the claims are heard.

Ringglass demand outruns what the extraction limits release, so there is always a buyer paying above the certified rate for an over-limit haul. The penalty for taking that work is a fine one profitable run absorbs, which is why determined operators keep taking it.

entities.name: Shear Compact

entities.description: Salvage operators formed the Shear Compact in 2383 around shared safety standards, neutral mediation, and the evidence from Shardfall.
entities.name: Shear Compact Formed

entities.description: Shei Lush is the pianist and Chair who has presided over Fermata Station's governing Sessions since 2424.

descriptiveIdentity.disposition: Shei restates a petitioner's business more exactly than they wrote it, and the room then argues her version. Where two proposals overlap she repeats their shared tones and withholds the note on which they differ.

facts.jurisdiction: Procedure and recognition during Fermata Sessions

gmNotes.text: Shei reads every submitted matter before a Session and restates the disputed change in her own words when the hearing opens. Petitioners hear their business summarized more exactly than they wrote it, and the Players then argue the version she stated.

Carry a point in a Session and Shei has a second ensemble play the resolution back before it enters the record. Anything that cannot be reproduced is written down as an adjournment, so an unrepeatable performance settles nothing.

The eastern seating bank returns a low tone under a full audience, so Shei has moved preliminary hearings to a smaller room and holds the central hall subject to [Ol'dent](/glass-frontier/entry/ol-dent)'s load tests. She refuses any tune whose load the hall cannot currently take.

entities.name: Shei Lush

entities.description: Fermata's Players chose Shei Lush as Chair in 2424 after a Session failed three times to determine its own adopted ending.
entities.name: Shei Lush Takes Chair

entities.description: Sideways Storm is Ashvane's recurrent lateral pressure front, bowing every rigid length above its current wavelength toward one fixed bearing and releasing the stored motion behind it.

descriptiveIdentity.signs: A dark pressure line crosses the horizon; survey boards post its lateral arrow and cutoff length while exposed frames begin bowing toward that bearing.
descriptiveIdentity.effects: Every continuous rigid member longer than the local wavelength stores the same sideways bend and releases it when the rear edge passes.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: Early breaks throw fragments across the front, while surviving towers, vessels, tools, and bones return through whatever occupies their original line.

facts.trigger: The charged front reaches a continuous rigid member longer than the pressure wavelength measured at that point on Ashvane
facts.effect: Every qualifying length bows toward the storm's fixed lateral bearing and stores the bend until the rear of the front passes
facts.recurrence: One front circles Ashvane through atmosphere, ground, and coupled structures, returning with the same lateral bearing while its local wavelength varies
facts.ending: A member snaps back as the rear edge passes unless it has broken, been shortened below the wavelength, or been latched in the bowed position
facts.mitigation: Build long frames in releasable sections, open their joints before arrival, or latch the stored bend into a controlled return
facts.anchor_behavior: Follows continuous rigid length rather than enclosed volume, crossing from ground into every coupled member long enough to take the load
facts.medium: Charged pressure moving through Ashvane's atmosphere, ground, structural frames, vehicles, and living bone
facts.content: A common lateral load stored in every continuous rigid length above the front's local wavelength
facts.hazard: The shared snapback can sweep landing fields, strike docks with their own vessels, misfire weapons, and break load-bearing frames or bones

gmNotes.text: Every continuous rigid object longer than the posted cutoff begins bowing toward the survey arrow, giving the scene one crossing of the front to release joints, latch a useful return, or clear its sweep.

entities.name: Sideways Storm

entities.description: The Signal Famine was the period of broken communication and isolated communities between the Glassfall in 2140 and sustained reconnection in 2305.
entities.name: Signal Famine

entities.description: Sithari is the largest city in the Kaleidos system, an equatorial surface capital built in layers above a surviving ring-era research campus.

descriptiveIdentity.setting: A dense, vertical, bright equatorial city of a few million, engineered crystal facades standing beside ring-era walls too useful to remove, built in layers over the buried campus that survived the Glassfall. Passing ring debris splits the daylight and lays moving bands of color across the streets, and a public stair can drop through several centuries of construction.
descriptiveIdentity.activity: The city writes, insures, translates, grades, and litigates: contracts spanning three jurisdictions, ringglass financed before it moves onward, colleges training the clerks and specialists who carry Sitharian standards outward. Government business runs in the measured phrasing of Sitharian, which can carry care, authority, and impatience at once.
descriptiveIdentity.access: Orbital shuttles and kites come down through Keelward's fields, and freight rail and city transit leave directly from the arrival halls.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: A central address names a surface entrance and a lowest public approach that may sit in different districts under different offices. Below the Underlayers' marked limit, active campus systems can change which corridors meet, and residents read an incoming debris drift off the facades before any public notice updates.

facts.population_band: A few million in the city proper
facts.role: De facto capital, financial centre and seat of the Tempered Accord
facts.setting: Equatorial surface city built in layers above a ring-era campus
facts.access: Orbital shuttles and the surface terminus of the Keel

gmNotes.text: A central Sithari address names a surface entrance and a lowest public approach, and the two can sit in different districts under different offices. A party given only one arrives at the wrong end of the right building.

When players plan around a posted schedule, the residents around them are already reading the color bands that passing debris lays across the facades, and they call a dense drift before the public notice updates.

Anything the party has graded, certified, financed, or ruled on here travels only as far as Sitharian institutions are trusted. A refusal issued in Sithari follows the document into every other jurisdiction.

entities.name: Sithari
entities.originBlurb: A surface capital where law, trade, and old institutions shape daily life.

entities.description: Sithari became the principal surface government and de facto system capital during the Rekindling in 2305.
entities.name: Sithari Becomes Capital

entities.description: Sithari's hardened research campus retained power and shelter through the Glassfall in 2140, drawing survivors inside its walls.
entities.name: Sithari Held The Glassfall

entities.description: The Six Returning Seals are the ceramic custody records fixed inside the Returning Pods. Their impressions reproduce the current tools, hands, and room tones of all eight Clearance desks despite older handling wear.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: Six palm-sized ceramic dockets, each with eight filled radial channels and handling wear older than the fresh restraint cloth surrounding it.
descriptiveIdentity.handling: Reading clockwise reproduces the current tools, hand pressures, and room tones of Clearance Eight's public desks in their proper order.
descriptiveIdentity.risks: The seals bind complete findings to evidence no desk witnessed. Treating their finished centers as ordinary authorization would close six claims around an unexplained custody sequence.

gmNotes.text: Every returned object arrived under a complete current seal, so the desks can release it only by accepting findings none of them remembers making.
Comparing a seal with its desk reproduces the same tool, hand pressure, and room tone while the older wear remains unchanged.
The seals are complete enough to close the claims and unexplained enough to keep them open, adding storage debt to every claimant.

entities.name: The Six Returning Seals

entities.description: Slate is a Crowncut labor dissident who alters shift tokens so injured salvagers can claim meals during disputes.
entities.name: Slate
entities.veilTagline: Slate recuts Crowncut shift tokens so injured salvagers can claim meals while their cases are disputed.

entities.description: Soma Irel is the former Waybearer who yielded his last occupied rescue road to Nalis Venn and now lives on Ashvane.

facts.specialty: Preparing travelers and defending an occupied crossing

gmNotes.text: Soma is waiting for an ordinary passage alongside the travelers and recognizes someone whose family crossed his last road; he needs help reaching them without reopening an old obligation.

entities.name: Soma Irel

entities.description: Soma's Last Road was the 2430 rescue from a captured freighter at Pelhari during which the Waybearer passed to Nalis Venn.

gmNotes.text: A survivor of the captive freighter asks for passage to someone who once pursued them across Soma's road and now wants to return a possession.

entities.name: Soma's Last Road

entities.description: Soma yielded the occupied rescue road to Nalis; he remained at the far end until the pursuers were captured.
entities.name: Somas Last Road Yielded

entities.description: Keepers compared distant esvar recordings whose divided-road figures coincided with the succession, before news of it reached their houses.
entities.name: Somas Road Seen Elsewhere

entities.description: Sora Meralis is Chief Ledgrist of the Echo Ledger Conclave, elected in 2433 after a career authenticating legal records.

descriptiveIdentity.disposition: Meralis gives a restricted holding's title, its date, and the reason it is closed, and not the recording. Her seals record the evidence she examined, the evidence she refused, and where a finding rests on interpretation.

facts.occupation: Chief Ledgrist of the Echo Ledger Conclave

gmNotes.text: Her catalogue corrections reach the party as paperwork trouble: one holding entered under two names, a gap nobody had listed, an access rule that differs between adjoining galleries they already have permission for.

Ask Meralis for a restricted holding and she gives the title, the date and the reason it is closed, without the recording. Private voices and the locations of active [Echo River](/glass-frontier/entry/kaleidos-echo-rivers) sites she refuses outright.

Three senior archivists have called a vote on her office while she keeps signing releases from [Thornvault](/glass-frontier/entry/thornvault)'s upper gallery. A sealed release survives her losing, so both sides of a dispute have reason to move before the ballots are counted.

entities.name: Sora Meralis

entities.description: South Shade is a road house below Shadewell's southern rim, where Ashvane's highland road meets the cargo lifts to the Keel fields.
