The Echo Ledger Conclave records the instrument output, the listener's transcript, and the conditions separately. Agreement among the three matters more than confidence in any one.

sections.heading: Custody
sections.text:
The [Echo Ledger Conclave](/glass-frontier/entry/echo-ledger-conclave) holds the largest catalog and authenticates fragments used in public claims. Ratter crews, hab archives, family collections, and private buyers hold the rest. Many transmissions circulate in several copies, each recovered from a different medium and each preserving different words.

New fragments still surface. Most add one ordinary detail to a place already known. Those details are often what make the old ring legible.

encyclopedia.summary: Old Traffic is signal traffic accidentally preserved in ringglass and crystal-bearing water since the intact ring age.
encyclopedia.title: Old Traffic

affordances: A coherent fragment can identify a speaker, place, or event and change a historical account.
cues: A loose crystal shard may carry a few seconds from the circuit it once served, and salvagers sell one by provenance and apparent clarity.
Fallen ring fragments can retain partial power and transmit on fixed intervals or remain silent until a Tuner supplies the missing carrier tone.
pressures: Repeated listening strengthens some patterns and erases others, while a listener can supply expected words across a gap without noticing.
variations: Routine traffic includes berth assignments, shift changes, repair requests, inventories, and weather notices.
Personal messages are rarer and often clearer, while technical strings are abundant and hard to place.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: A lean, short-furred, dog-shaped animal in gallery gray, encountered mid-wall or overhead at an unhurried trot — level, comfortable, and oriented to a floor that stopped being one at the Glassfall.
descriptiveIdentity.behavior: It follows the ring's original alignment wherever it goes — walking old floors through new gravities, resting in corners that were corners, drinking, when it drinks, from water it laps sideways off a seep — and it moves through inhabited country on long repeated rounds.
descriptiveIdentity.threat: An olddown carries ordinary weight on an unexpected surface. People below its overhead route clear loose objects and give it room at junctions, where two definitions of floor can cross.
descriptiveIdentity.senses: Olddowns thread changed sections along courses matching old deck plans and stop at the former position of doorways even when the frame is buried or gone.
descriptiveIdentity.risks: An olddown may wait for days at a sealed former passage. Restoration crews verify the old plan and inspect the present structure before deciding whether to reopen it.

facts.origin: Documented in hab galleries and fragment interiors since the earliest postfall records; the survey literature's founding observation — that every olddown's private down matches the ring's original orientation for that section — has held through every survey since
facts.biology: A lean, short-furred, dog-shaped animal by every external measure, whose weight simply answers a different down — it stands on whatever surface the ring's original orientation makes a floor, walks spin-country walls at an unhurried trot, and rests curled in corners that were corners once
facts.lifespan: Unestablished; marked individuals persist across survey generations, and no observed birth, growth stage, or death fixes the limits
facts.function: An olddown's stance gives the original ring alignment of its current section; restoration trades compare that bearing with recovered plans and structural surveys
facts.resonance_relation: The animal presses its chosen surface with ordinary weight, but instruments have not detected the force that holds it to the section's former down

sections.heading: Main
sections.text:
An olddown is lean, short-furred, dog-shaped, and aligned to the ring's former down — old down in the restoration trades. In a fragment whose tumble made walls of floors, it walks along the surface that served as floor before the Glassfall. Its paws press with ordinary weight. Surveys have not detected the holding force, but repeated measurements place the stance to the original orientation of each section.

Olddowns travel long rounds through galleries and wreck interiors. They rest in former corners, lap seep water from the side that used to lie below it, and pass through old door positions in the sequence shown on recovered plans. At a blocked or vanished doorway, an animal may wait for days before reversing its route. Marked individuals repeat these paths across survey generations. Birth, growth, feeding, and death remain undocumented in the available observation record.

Restoration crews use an olddown's stance to check recovered plans and follow its rounds to identify lost corridor geometry. Hab residents leave resting corners clear and route traffic around an animal walking overhead. When an olddown waits at a sealed passage, crews inspect both the old plan and the present structure. Some reopen the former doorway when it can be done safely; others mark the position and leave it closed.

encyclopedia.summary: Olddowns are lean dog-shaped anomalies whose weight follows the original ring orientation of each section they enter. They walk former floors through changed gravity, rest at old corners, and pause where vanished doorways once opened.
encyclopedia.title: Olddowns

affordances: An olddown's stance preserves the former down of each ring section, while its repeated route marks old corridors and doorway positions for comparison with surveys.
cues: The olddown trots overhead down the gallery's wall at its unhurried pace — level to a floor that stopped being one at the Glassfall — and foot traffic bends around its route with the ease of long custom.
The restoration crew checks the rebuilt junction the trade's way — asking the dog — and the olddown's stance, set against the new decking, reads two degrees of error the instruments missed.
variations: Gallery olddowns range settled habs and are known individually; the fragment-wreck populations of the debris fields walk old alignments through open ruin, and salvage crews chart their rounds as free survey.
Survey literature compares relict maintenance fauna and a postfall anomaly as origin models. The measured alignment and repeated rounds support neither model by themselves.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: A folded animal resembles a loose brown lining; spread open, its translucent edge surrounds a dark toothed seam.
descriptiveIdentity.behavior: An anchored adult unfolds across disturbed water and curls its adhesive face around a struggling body.
descriptiveIdentity.threat: Large specimens entangle hands and sampling tools, pulling them against a concealed feeding groove.
descriptiveIdentity.senses: Water displacement and contact trigger the closing movement.

facts.biology: A broad muscular ribbon with an adhesive inner face, a toothed feeding groove and a tough anchoring disc
facts.principal_accommodation: Pressurized liquid brine and a continuing supply of small animals in a sheltered seep

sections.heading: Main
sections.text:
The ometh specimens described from [Oravel](/glass-frontier/entry/oravel)'s lower brine fissures were first mistaken for detached Ovri skins. A resting animal gathers its ribbon around an anchoring disc and hangs against the wall. Small swimmers shelter among the folds. When a larger disturbance reaches it, the ribbon opens across the water and closes on whatever touches its inner face.

Adhesion holds prey against a feeding groove running down the body. Pulling straight away stretches the ribbon and draws that groove closer. A broad plate slid beneath a caught edge can peel it back; cutting the anchor releases the animal without releasing its grip. Excavators who reach blindly through warm flooded openings risk fastening an ometh to their own arm. The animal cannot pursue them across exposed frozen ground, but the shelter needed to save an injured companion also keeps the predator alive.

[Daret Valis](/glass-frontier/entry/daret-valis)'s field drawings distinguish the stationary anchoring disc from the soft folds around it. At [Ithara](/glass-frontier/entry/ithara), buyers have paid for intact adults in deep cases, hoping to study the wet adhesive. Empty cases with scored interiors also circulate. The known captures establish this predator in some warm cavities; they give no measure of the extent or variety of Lithren's surviving enclosed waters.

encyclopedia.summary: Ometh are folded ribbon predators in Lithren's enclosed warm brines, anchoring to a cavity wall while a broad adhesive body closes around prey.
encyclopedia.title: Ometh

affordances: A visible anchoring disc gives a careful observer a way to distinguish a resting predator from a shed microbial skin.
cues: A brown lining lifts away from the wall, revealing a pale disc that remains firmly attached.
The loose ribbon wraps the sampler; a dark seam turns slowly toward the trapped grip.
pressures: Freeing the anchor makes the animal portable while leaving its adhesive grip intact.
variations: Small ometh catch swimmers in folds no wider than a hand.
Large adults spread across a narrow fissure, leaving an apparently clear opening above their folded feeding surface.

descriptiveIdentity.manner: The answering bench gives first attempts priority on the chalk board, brings the room in under a faltering player, and holds silence when the named song calls for it.
descriptiveIdentity.attire: Ordinary best, plus settlement-colored sashes for the answering bench; players claim the empty chair without a separate mark.
descriptiveIdentity.hospitality: Every open door owes a stranger a seat and a listen; a traveling player who names a song from their own country is answered by the bench's best approximation, and the mangled answer, warmly meant, is by long custom the festival's favorite joke.

facts.integration: Most settlements with session culture keep the festival on their own date; the answering-bench roles rotate among respected locals, and a town's festival manners are considered as legible a civic reference as its docks
facts.formal_register: The festival's forms are called aloud — a player claims a song by naming it to the bench, the bench opens the room's answer, and the closing of a session is the bench's line, 'the room thanks the players,' delivered once and ending the night
facts.aesthetic: Answering-bench sashes in the settlement's colors, the chalked session boards outside every open door listing what has been played and what has been promised, and the tradition's one fixed decoration: an empty chair in every session room, kept for whoever has yet to stand up

sections.heading: Main
sections.text:
During the Open, first-timers and established players claim songs from the same chalked board. Every room keeps an empty chair for the next person to stand. Its answering bench consists of sashed locals appointed for the night. They cue a sung response, bring the audience under a faltering singer, hold silence for listening songs, and time stamped choruses or laughter. The bench treats the audience as one part of the performance.

The festival grows from the Answering Phrase, practiced year-round. A player names the song to the bench; the bench opens the room's answer. At closing, it says *the room thanks the players* once, and the chalked board stays outside the door until morning. Fermata uses callers and runs until the ferries. Cold settlements sing in stove shifts, while dock towns add the songs of crews currently in port. Promise columns on the boards record songs people will learn for the next year's rooms.

encyclopedia.summary: The Open is an annual night when every session room, gallery, and market floor opens to any player. Appointed answering benches lead each audience's sung, silent, stamped, or spoken response under the rule: the room answers.
encyclopedia.title: The Open

affordances: The empty chair gives a first-time player a guaranteed place, while the promise board carries new songs into the next year's repertoire.
cues: The first-timer stands at the empty chair and names her song to the bench in a voice that nearly fails — and the bench brings the room in under her second verse so smoothly that the nearly-failing becomes the story everyone tells about the year she started.

At the night's end the sashed bench stands, says the one line — the room thanks the players — and the chalked board outside the door is left up until morning, played songs on one side, promises on the other.
variations: Fermata's runs on its callers and ends with the ferries; cold settlements sing in stove shifts; dock towns absorb the port's crews and keep their songs — the law and the empty chair are everywhere the same.

The benches' embroidered line — a song is half whoever answers it — travels home with visiting players, and settlements new to session culture typically adopt the festival first and grow the year-round rooms up under it.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: Orcs are tall and broad, dense through the bone, with skin in deep saturated tones — charcoals, greens, rich earths — that catch light. Past their physical prime they tend to stiffen rather than lose mass.
descriptiveIdentity.senses: Orcish pain response is muted: damage underreports itself, and an orc can work through an injury they genuinely have not noticed. What orcs read keenly is material under stress — how a loaded seam or a ringglass-laced alloy wants to move under their hands.

facts.origin: Alien arrivals during the ring era
facts.biology: Dense bones, heavy musculature, high endurance and muted pain response
facts.lifespan: Comparable to humans, with an earlier peak and steeper decline
facts.resonance_relation: Strong material sense; best suited to structural and kinetic work

encyclopedia.originBlurb: Dense-boned and enduring, orcs read resonance most readily through stressed metal, stone, and glass.

sections.heading: Main
sections.text: Orcs arrived from outside Kaleidos during the ring era. Surviving arrival records disagree over their order relative to the human landings, but civic and trade records place established orc households throughout the ring-era system.

sections.heading: Biology
sections.text:
Orc physiology combines dense bone, heavy musculature, and efficient sustained effort. Average lifespan is comparable to a human's, with an earlier physical peak followed by a steeper loss of joint flexibility and muscle elasticity. Older orcs often retain mass while becoming stiff and sore.

Orcish pain response is muted. Damage may register as mild discomfort, allowing an injured person to continue working through a fracture or early resonance exposure. Field medics therefore use inspection and instrument readings instead of asking pain level alone.

Orcs are tall and broad, with skin in deep saturated tones including charcoals, greens, and rich earths. Individual appearance varies across the cultures and populations of the system.

sections.heading: The Stereotype
sections.text:
Orcs have no shared species culture or homeland. Communication, art, apprenticeship, and public standing follow the cultures and institutions in which a person was raised. Claims that all orcs speak with one direct register or share one temperament are stereotypes applied across populations with different languages and customs.

Some orc-majority workshop communities preserve long apprenticeships built on repetition, exact standards, blunt critique, and destruction of work that fails examination. Their metalwork and structurally complex music have reputations beyond those communities. Other orc workers train under local trade practices, and neither method follows from biology.

sections.heading: Relationship with Resonance
sections.text: Orcish resonance sense is strongest through material under stress: the movement of a loaded seam, the response of ringglass-laced alloy, and the vibration a crystal structure carries into the hands. Structural and kinetic practice uses that tactile information directly. Frequency architecture and harmonic modeling remain learned disciplines supported by instruments, shared theory, and collaborators with other sensory strengths.

sections.heading: Present Day
sections.text: Orcs live throughout the system without a species-level homeland or cultural center. An orc raised in Sithari belongs to Sithari's culture; an orc raised in a ring hab inherits that hab's customs. Orc-majority neighborhoods and workshops maintain institutions specific to their settlement and trade.

encyclopedia.summary: Orcs are a sapient ring-era immigrant species whose dense bones, heavy musculature, and high endurance suit structural and kinetic resonance work.
encyclopedia.title: Orcs

affordances: Orcish endurance and sensitivity to material under stress suit prolonged physical work and structural or kinetic resonance craft.
cues: An orc is tall and broad, dense through the bone, with skin in deep saturated tones and strong, precisely proportioned features.
An injured or overexposed orc often reports less pain than the damage warrants and may continue working through a hidden fracture.
pressures: Muted pain hides injury and early resonance exposure, while age brings a steep loss of flexibility after an earlier physical peak.
variations: Orcs belong primarily to the cultures that raised them and have no single species homeland or cultural center.
Some orc-majority workshops preserve demanding traditions of repetition and exact standards; other orc workers train in the methods of their local culture and trade.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: Human-scaled and visibly weight-set — an oruun settled to heavy spin reads dense and planted, one settled light moves with a floating economy — with the exchanged rings worn at wrist or ear, their weights legible to any oruun at a glance.
descriptiveIdentity.senses: During acclimation, changes in tissue tension make local spin, trim, and gradual drift readily felt. This does not confer a special sense of resonance bands.
descriptiveIdentity.behavior: An acclimating oruun eats more, rests often, and changes gait as tissue density settles. Spinway households commonly plan travel around this interval and use weighted rings to mark chosen bonds.

facts.origin: A people of the spinways; the ring-era censuses record oruun communities settled through the spin-graded districts, and the fragments' registries record them everywhere weight varies
facts.biology: Density-adaptive tissue — skin, muscle, and bone shifting mass and set over days to match local spin — with the settling felt and described by oruun as the body 'agreeing' with a place
facts.lifespan: About 70–120 years
facts.resonance_relation: Density adaptation responds to weight and spin, while resonance-band work requires learned practice and instruments; an acclimating oruun feels small trim changes through tissue tension

encyclopedia.originBlurb: Skin, muscle, and bone adjust their density over several days to match local spin.

sections.heading: Main
sections.text:
Oruun skin, muscle, and bone change density over several days to match local spin. Oruun call the process *agreeing*. Under heavier spin the frame becomes denser and the stance more planted; under lighter spin it sheds mass and changes leverage. The transition increases appetite and fatigue and can disturb balance until gait and tissue settle together. Rapid movement between grades can make an oruun seriously ill, so travel schedules include acclimation time.

The adaptation made oruun common in the ring's spin-graded districts and remains useful among fragments that maintain different gravities. It does not make travel immediate: an acclimating worker needs food, rest, and time, and a settled body is optimized for its current grade. Small trim changes become perceptible through tissue tension during the process, so dock and hab crews often ask an oruun colleague to compare that feeling with the posted logs.

Spinway communities developed weighted-ring exchanges among several customs of chosen kinship. Two people select and exchange rings whose weight marks how they describe the bond; a returned ring is traditionally melted. Households spread across several spin grades often meet at weight-neutral fairs where no one arrives fully acclimated to another's home. Neither the rings nor dispersed households define oruun life throughout Kaleidos, but both remain recognizable practices along the old spinways.

encyclopedia.summary: Oruun are a sapient people whose skin, muscle, and bone adjust their density to local spin over several days. The adaptation supports life across Kaleidos's many gravity grades but makes rapid changes between them physically taxing.
encyclopedia.title: Oruun

affordances: An acclimated oruun can live and work comfortably across Kaleidos's common spin grades, and can feel small trim changes through tissue tension while settling.
cues: The dock clerk turns her wrist to show the weight of an exchanged ring; the newcomer answers with his own before they name the bond each ring records.

Two days after arriving, the oruun surveyor stops mid-step on the gallery and says the spin is out a quarter-point — and the habmaster, who has learned what a settling body is worth, sends for the trim logs.
pressures: Settling takes several days. Rapid transfers between spin grades cause fatigue, imbalance, and serious illness, so travel and work begin with an acclimation interval.
variations: Ring-exchange kinship binds by chosen weight — heavy rings for the bonds meant to anchor, light for the ones meant to travel — and a broken bond returns its ring, by custom, melted.
Some spinway households maintain kin across several gravity grades and meet at weight-neutral fairs. Other oruun households remain in one settlement for generations.

sections.heading: Main
sections.text:
Orveks fold around a rock edge as a sequence of short gripping plates. Each plate can turn independently before the links take load. A climber fastens the brace, pulls from the intended direction and watches which plates settle. The joints keep a long continuous rigid member out of equipment used around Ashvane's [Sideways Storm](/glass-frontier/entry/sideways-storm); the brace still depends on the strength and shape of the rock it grips.

Travelers in [Eshrel](/glass-frontier/entry/eshrel) use orveks to secure themselves below refuge roofs and to board [Uldevan](/glass-frontier/entry/uldevan) when its steps stand above an uneven landing. Fine grit packs between the plates. A brace that folds freely in the shop can refuse to conform after an exposed crossing, leaving only one plate carrying its apparent grip.

Imported sets have reached the wet cliffs beneath [Charethis](/glass-frontier/entry/charethis) and the exterior carvings of [Aldevra](/glass-frontier/entry/aldevra). Soft pads protect worked stone but lose purchase under slime; pointed plates hold rough rock while damaging ornament. Climbers choose which loss they can accept. A linked pair can make a hanging seat for a long wait, provided the second brace rests on a genuinely separate support.

encyclopedia.summary: An orvek is an Ashvane climbing brace made from short independent gripping plates joined by flexible load-bearing links.
encyclopedia.title: Orvek

affordances: An orvek provides a removable hold around an irregular edge without carrying a long rigid climbing member.
cues: A folded strip opens into several small jaws, each turning to meet a different face of the rock.
A climber shakes hot grit from the links before trusting the brace with their weight.
variations: Ashvane sets leave wide clearances between short heat-resistant plates.
Wet-cliff sets use replaceable soft pads and drain openings, with pointed plates carried separately for rough stone.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: A pale, flat-bodied hunter longer than a person, with six hooked limbs and a folding jaw beneath a shield of dark bony plates.
descriptiveIdentity.behavior: Hangs beneath shelves and tracks footfalls through its hooked feet; eggs adhere in translucent clusters above warm seeps.
descriptiveIdentity.threat: Braces its plates through a local structural resonance while gripping rock, then releases that defense to leap onto moving prey.

sections.heading: Main
sections.text:
Oshrets hunt the deep caverns of Korvath's uplands. An adult can flatten against a ceiling with its limbs folded around the edge of a shelf. Its pale underside resembles mineral flow; the open jaw is dark and fringed with inward teeth. It drops onto prey and hooks the stone again before feeding.

The feet register vibrations through rock. Small scavengers disturb the ground too little to be worth a leap, while boots and heavy digging machinery bring a hunter toward a worked passage. Oshrets sometimes follow the same drill for days, waiting above the place where its operators step off the machine.

sections.heading: The Grip
sections.text:
An oshret's gripping limbs brace its bony shield through structural resonance. Rounds that should penetrate can chip the plate without reaching flesh. The brace fails when the animal loses contact with continuous rock. A hanging mesh, a swinging platform or a fall leaves it vulnerable, as does the interval between releasing its feet and landing a leap. Its soft jaw and limb joints remain exposed even while it holds fast.

Hunters use vibrating decoys to draw an animal over a gap. Shots and explosions travel through the cavern and can summon another hunter behind the first. Fire drives adults away from their eggs until the heat becomes dangerous to the clutch; then they rush the source. The animals do not follow spoken commands, and no known bond makes a nest a tame weapon.

sections.heading: Deral's Returning Hunters
sections.text:
At [Deral](/glass-frontier/entry/deral), [Oru](/glass-frontier/entry/oru) has survived a hanging-net trap and changed its approach. The [Deral Hunters](/glass-frontier/entry/deral-hunters) compare its movements with those of other adults before carrying a familiar trick into a new passage. The mine's warm seeps support both prey and attached clutches; clearing one worked chamber leaves adjoining breeding ground intact.

An offer from [House Tereval](/glass-frontier/entry/house-tereval) has made living eggs valuable to rescuers short of passage. The [Ilvaren](/glass-frontier/entry/ilvaren) can advise on receiving enclosures, but a warm case suited to eggs may be easily climbed or broken by hatchlings. The argument concerns the particular clutch and its destination. It has not made the hunters abandon people still trapped beyond the nests.

encyclopedia.summary: Oshrets are large climbing predators of Korvath's upland caverns, able to brace themselves against gunfire while gripping continuous stone.
encyclopedia.title: Oshret

affordances: Drawing an oshret onto suspended flooring breaks the rock contact that hardens its shield.
cues: A ceiling's pale mineral fold draws its edges inward as footsteps approach, exposing hooked feet.
Fresh bullet chips surround a resting hunter whose shield remains intact; the soft jaw hangs unprotected beneath it.
pressures: A loud attempt to kill one hunter brings footfall-sensitive adults along adjoining rock, including the ceiling behind the party.
variations: Young hunters occupy narrow cracks adults cannot enter; egg-bearing nests defend warm seeps instead of pursuing distant prey.
An isolated hunter follows quarry machinery; a breeding group stays near its cavern and attacks intruders from several heights.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: A narrow folding bar holds two detachable heads, each with a bright split-circle target and a hooded eyepiece.
descriptiveIdentity.working: The heads exchange low-power light along a visible path; paired readings expose movement or incompatible geometry.
descriptiveIdentity.risks: Dust, reflections and moving supports corrupt a reading; a reflected target can appear to be the head itself.

facts.function: Compares angles and light travel between two marked heads to measure a visible gap and detect disagreement between the ends
facts.operating_limit: Needs a clear optical path and stable supports; it measures the path light takes and cannot establish that a distorted route is safe to cross

sections.heading: Main
sections.text:
An othel opens from a short case into a bar with a detachable head at each end. Together they measure small gaps and check whether a fitted piece sits square. Separated onto stable supports, they compare a crossing from both sides. A split-circle target makes a displaced head obvious through the opposite eyepiece. The instrument uses low-power light rather than sounding the surrounding material with resonance.

[Tamet](/glass-frontier/entry/tamet) uses othels in [Ithara](/glass-frontier/entry/ithara)'s repair work, and excavators carry them into [Damarat](/glass-frontier/entry/damarat). A head placed on fixed rock can reveal that a nearby roof is still moving even when its motion cannot be seen by eye. Cheap instruments display one averaged result. Field patterns preserve the readings from both heads so a disagreement remains visible.

Crews aboard [Quiet Measure](/glass-frontier/entry/quiet-measure) use paired readings before extending a passage toward a damaged vessel near [Pell Cut](/glass-frontier/entry/pell-cut). In the Shear, light and people may follow different paths through a distorted space. A neat measured distance is therefore one observation among others. A false image or polished corner can also return the target from the wrong direction. Moving one head sideways exposes many ordinary reflections without requiring anyone to cross the gap.

encyclopedia.summary: An othel is a portable optical measuring instrument whose separable heads compare a narrow crossing or cavity from both ends without an active resonance pulse.
encyclopedia.title: Othel

affordances: Separated heads compare an opening from both ends while observers remain on stable ground.
cues: The two eyepieces show different distances across the same open doorway.
A split circle slides apart as the roof settles, although the fitted beam still looks level.
variations: Bench othels stay on their folding bar and favor close fitting work.
Field sets have independent mounts and preserve separate readings, exposing disagreement that cheaper displays smooth away.

sections.heading: Main
sections.text:
Othri flatten their narrow bodies to enter the branching growth on a Nereth's back. Several adults attend young in the same sheltered channels. When another swimmer approaches, the adults rush outward together, striking exposed skin with hard mouth plates. Their host continues grazing while the fish retreat into its burden.

At [Lake Othrel](/glass-frontier/entry/lake-othrel), fishers recognize occupied growth by the silver flashes at its openings. A carried object can hide an entire nursery. Divers who put fingers into an apparently empty handle sometimes draw a defensive rush before they can withdraw. Supporting a loose branch in a water-filled basket lets the fish leave it gradually; taking it straight onto the ice strands both eggs and adults.

Shore households preserve adult othri for sale in [Ladderwell](/glass-frontier/entry/ladderwell). They catch free-swimming groups among the shallows and leave heavily occupied hosts alone while the young are small. Other lakes have populations sheltering in submerged roots and stone holes. These fish form smaller guarding groups, and keepers moving them into a display pool must supply several separate recesses if they want the adults to stop fighting over one doorway.

encyclopedia.summary: Othri are cold-lake fish that shelter their young inside the porous back growth of nereth and defend those cavities in coordinated rushes.
encyclopedia.title: Othri

affordances: Nurseries identify occupied passages within a grazer's burden; free-swimming adults provide a valued local food.
cues: Silver bodies vanish into the same opening in a grazer's back, then burst out together toward an approaching hand.
Tiny fish crowd the wet interior of a shed branch lying on the shore ice.
variations: Nereth-associated groups travel with their hosts and defend several connected chambers.
Root-dwelling populations keep small fixed territories and return to familiar recesses after feeding.

descriptiveIdentity.signs: Speech acquires a second tone, machine lights align to the speaker's pulse, and the commanded subject repeats the operative words before acting.

facts.effect: Compel one person, creature, or machine that receives and understands the words to perform one immediate, physically possible action
facts.limits: The spell supplies neither knowledge nor skill, cannot establish a standing order, and follows the subject's literal understanding rather than the practitioner's unspoken intent
facts.consequence: One recent autobiographical memory becomes inaccessible until the action ends; if the subject resists the command, that memory does not return

sections.heading: Main
sections.text:
Three Forms teaching calls the spell *Outside Will*: Will imposed from beyond a subject's own Form. One person, creature, or machine receives one command to perform one immediate act. The command must be heard or otherwise received, understood, and physically possible. It can stop a hand in mid-strike, turn one mounted weapon, or make a constructed servant open the place it guards.

Outside Will provides obedience rather than competence. A subject ordered to fly a vessel cannot do so without the relevant skill. A machine ordered to identify a liar cannot answer unless it has a way to make that judgment. The spell cannot wait as policy or standing instruction: when the immediate act ends, so does the command.

sections.heading: The Price of Authority
sections.text:
Casting Outside Will closes one recent autobiographical memory to the practitioner: the last meal, a route walked that morning, the reason a tool was in hand. The memory returns when the compelled act ends unless the subject resisted. Resistance makes the absence permanent even when the command succeeds.

[The Red Sovereign](/glass-frontier/entry/red-sovereign) extends Outside Will into standing and collective command, with a cost that follows the betrayals it compels.

encyclopedia.summary: Outside Will imposes a comprehensible command on minds, machines, or constructed servants and holds them to its exact terms.
encyclopedia.title: Outside Will

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: Purple-black folds beneath pale mineral crust; a wet cut exposes thin copper-colored layers.
descriptiveIdentity.behavior: New skins advance along supplied fissures while dry outer folds harden and split away.
descriptiveIdentity.threat: An exposed colony can lose the fluid pressure that keeps its interior liquid; hot mineral spray may follow a broken crust.
descriptiveIdentity.senses: Local changes in chemistry and flow govern growth; the mat has no observed organs for following people.
descriptiveIdentity.risks: A dry surface can conceal living layers and pressurized brine directly beneath it.

facts.biology: Interdependent microbes in a fibrous matrix, sustained by chemical differences between fresh seep fluid and the surrounding mineral deposits
facts.principal_accommodation: Liquid brine, retained pressure and a continuing supply of warm reactive fluid beneath an insulating crust

sections.heading: Main
sections.text:
Lithren excavators call the flexible dark growth inside some enclosed seeps ovri. A colony consists of many kinds of minute organism held in a fibrous matrix. Fresh fluid brings dissolved compounds from warmer rock. Reactions along the boundary with older deposits supply the energy used to build more matrix. New layers creep around the seep while mineral grains accumulate in the older ones.

Living ovri requires liquid brine. Rock, ice and the colony's own crust retain its pressure; heat arrives with the fluid. On the open surface, an exposed wet fold loses fluid and freezes. Pale flakes caught in frost may therefore come from a living chamber below, but a carpet of flakes does not make the country above it habitable. A pressure probe and a sample of the fluid tell an excavator more than the color of the exposed crust.

The modern word distinguishes ovri skins, ovri brine and dead ovri crust in specimen accounts. Those are parts of one living association. Samples from separate seeps differ in salinity, mineral content and the organisms most abundant in them. Their presence establishes a surviving local ecology. No recovered sequence connects its beginning to the ruins' builders or to Lithren's former climate.

sections.heading: A Skin Worth Bringing Back
sections.text:
Cleaned outer skins remain flexible when kept damp. Instrument makers use small sheets to separate brines that would rapidly clog a woven filter. The different colonies pass dissolved materials at different rates; a purchaser wants a tested sample and its fluid, not a sack of dry purple scraps. Dried skins curl into hard scales and lose that useful behavior.

A small side sample can be removed under a sealed hood while leaving the main flow enclosed. Stripping the whole roof gives more material at once but can drain the pocket and kill its exposed living layers. Collectors who retain pressure can follow the wet edge into adjoining cavities. A colony has no interest in keeping a passage open: its next skin may grow over the slit used on the previous visit.

Quiet seeps build thick nested bowls around small openings. Faster flows stretch the skins into long hanging pockets, whose motion reveals a pulse arriving from deeper rock. Both forms can include mineral casts left by folds that have already died. Dating a crust dates that deposited layer, not the age of every living patch attached to it.

sections.heading: Kavren and the Traveling Samples
sections.text:
[Kavren](/glass-frontier/entry/kavren), the colony in [Oravel](/glass-frontier/entry/oravel)'s western cut, supplies a closely observed example. The [Ithara Comparative Expedition](/glass-frontier/entry/ithara-comparative-expedition) compares small hooded samples with material brought from other enclosed seeps. A collector using a Neral can preserve the sample's fluid while leaving the main flow covered. The hard flakes gathered outside the pocket travel separately as Ovri Scales.

Living material at [Ithara](/glass-frontier/entry/ithara) is kept in wet pressurized cases. Differences between those cases and their source seeps matter when comparing skins: a poorly fed transported mat may behave differently from the colony it came from. Sellers who bring a sketch of the sampled fold and its neighboring layers give buyers something to compare against the changed specimen.

encyclopedia.summary: Ovri are layered living mats in Lithren's enclosed brine seeps, building flexible mineral skins around the warm fluid that feeds them.
encyclopedia.title: Ovri

affordances: A wet growth edge traces a supplied fissure; following it under retained pressure can reveal a cavity beyond the visible seep.
Tested living skins can separate mineral-rich fluids for instruments, making an intact sample worth transporting cold and wet.
cues: A pale flake turns over under the lamp, showing a purple inner face and a wet copper-colored seam.
Inside an enclosed crack, soft folds lift together when a pulse of brine reaches them, then settle against their mineral casing.
variations: Slow pockets grow nested bowls whose dry outer rims can be sampled without exposing the main flow.
Fast seeps stretch long pockets across openings; tearing one may empty the space that supports all the neighboring folds.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: Pale curled flakes with purple inner faces and brittle copper-colored edges.
descriptiveIdentity.working: Nested dry scales leave small sheltered gaps; cloth sleeves hold them apart around an instrument.
descriptiveIdentity.risks: Crushing destroys their spacing, and scales taken from a live roof can conceal a pressurized seep beneath.

facts.function: Overlapping curled scales trap still gas and cushion a rigid case's contents
facts.grades: Broad whole curls for packing; crushed stock for loose fill; wet skins retained separately as living material

sections.heading: Main
sections.text:
Dead Ovri skins curl as they dry. Around enclosed seeps on [Lithren](/glass-frontier/entry/lithren), frost carries loose scales into sheltered hollows where collectors can gather them without opening the wet growth below. Their mineral faces are hard, but a loosely nested handful compresses like a bed of springs. Sewn into sleeves, the curls cushion glass and trap still gas inside a pressurized case. They provide little insulation in an evacuated space.

Crews at [Oravel](/glass-frontier/entry/oravel) collect already detached stock around [Kavren](/glass-frontier/entry/kavren). In [Ithara](/glass-frontier/entry/ithara), a bag of sound broad curls is an ordinary packing purchase. [Tamet](/glass-frontier/entry/tamet) uses replaceable sleeves around delicate forming pieces; a broken sleeve spills conspicuous purple flakes across the bench. Damp stock must be dried before packing or its salts can stain and corrode the object it protects.

Scales no longer perform the selective filtration of living ovri skins. A seller offering dry packing as a living filter is selling the wrong material. Whole curls remain useful through several journeys if shaken clear and left uncrushed. Powder from a damaged sleeve has little spring and belongs outside the next instrument case. Crews sometimes recognize a opened cargo by the pale flakes clinging to a thief's cuffs.

encyclopedia.summary: Ovri scales are the curled dead outer skins of Lithren's brine mats, gathered as light mineral packing for cold instruments and specimen cases.
encyclopedia.title: Ovri Scales

affordances: Dry whole scales provide locally available protective packing without requiring a live colony to be opened.
cues: Purple-faced curls fall from a torn padded sleeve and spring apart across the floor.
A collector lifts loose pale flakes while leaving the wet seam beneath them covered.
variations: Broad curls fill removable sleeves around fragile instruments.
Small flakes settle into loose fill that needs frequent turning and replacement as it crushes.

descriptiveIdentity.signs: The room moves smoothly with clean boundaries and no preceding local disturbance; its registered partner records simultaneous movement of the same extent in the opposite direction.
descriptiveIdentity.effects: The pair moves in balance — drift answered by inverse drift, gain by loss — and the two districts' wardens compare logs afterward that match, line for line, with the signs reversed.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: A forced or accidental slip at one end can move the partner without local warning; current registers let wardens warn the second district and clear both rooms together.

facts.medium: Paired elven fabric in the displacement zones — chambers and sections whose position-keeping was built to reconcile jointly, and still does, wherever both halves of a pairing survive
facts.nature: A conserved exchange: displacement arrives in the pair as equal and opposite movement — one room's drift, turn, or insertion answered by its partner's inverse — the two reconciling like linked accounts whatever distance separates them
facts.hazard: The pairing transmits trouble as faithfully as balance — a slip forced or triggered at one end arrives at the other on the partner's schedule, in a district that felt neither cause nor warning
facts.known_forms: Charted stable pairs with repeatable matched movement; orphan slips whose missing partners leave irregular displacement; and chained events in which movement passes through several surviving pairs

sections.heading: Main
sections.text:
Pairing moves two chambers at once. One room's drift, turn, or insertion is matched by equal movement in the opposite direction at its partner, sometimes districts or fragments away. Warden logs from both ends match in time and extent with their directions reversed. Surviving paired sections are found in elven fabric whose position-keeping systems were joined; the link continues across the present distance between the fragments.

Every displacement-zone register carries a partner column, exchanged between districts each season. When one room slips, its wardens warn the listed partner district before entering either chamber. Stable pairs can be scheduled around and some storage operators use their repeatable balance. Forced movement at one end also reaches the other, so work on a paired room requires both districts to clear their sites. Orphan slips, whose partners were lost with other fragments, move irregularly and remain under watch. In rare chained events, one slip passes through several paired sections; afterward the services compare times and movements to extend the network map.

encyclopedia.summary: Pairing is the simultaneous displacement of two surviving sections of elven fabric in equal and opposite directions, even across districts or fragments. Zone wardens keep partner registers because movement or interference at one room can reach the other.
encyclopedia.title: Pairing

affordances: A charted movement at one end forecasts the partner's direction and extent, allowing both districts to clear rooms and coordinate storage or survey work.
cues: The parlor slips with the smooth, clean-edged movement the wardens call bookkept, and the district office's first act is the partner column — then the courtesy call two fragments over: your entry just posted.
The two wardens lay their logs side by side at the season comparison — drift for inverse drift, line for reversed line — and initial the match, one more season of the old fabric keeping its books.
pressures: Work that forces one room to move can displace its partner without local warning, so paired sites require joint clearance and current cross-district registers.
variations: Stable pairs are logged like tides; orphan slips with lost partners move strangely and are watched; and the chained events that run whole pairing networks are the zones' great catastrophes, mapped afterward and drilled against since.

Pairings ignore present-day borders — partners sit in different districts, jurisdictions, and fragments — and the cross-zone register comparisons each season are one of the quiet arrangements the displacement authorities keep above all their other politics.

descriptiveIdentity.signs: The taster holds a bare shard near the mouth, breathes across it once, closes their eyes for the length of a swallow, and names grade, vein, and often the quarry — then rinses with the plain water every tasting bench keeps ready.
descriptiveIdentity.effect: Each grade and vein of ringglass leaves its own metallic trace on the breath, and a born taster reads the trace to a fineness the survey instruments confirm on the bench in an afternoon what the mouth called in a breath.
descriptiveIdentity.limits: The gift runs in the Kyther tasting lines and arrives with the family's other features or skips a child entirely. Training refines what birth supplies, and a taster's palate fatigues by mid-shift, so trade tastings are scheduled in the morning with water between lots.

facts.function: Grades ringglass by the metallic trace it leaves on the breath, to a fineness instruments match slowly and expensively

sections.heading: Main
sections.text:
In the Kyther tasting families, *palate* means the inherited sense by which ringglass has flavors. The gift arrives with the family features or skips a child entirely and reads the metallic trace a bare shard leaves on the breath finely enough to name grade, vein, and often the quarry in the length of a swallow. The survey bench confirms the call in an afternoon of instrument time. The range's stock trade runs on it: quarry lots are tasted before they are priced, the tasting families' verdicts travel with the stock like assay marks, and the great buyers pay for a taster's breath the way archives pay for a recaller's wrist.

Tasting families keep pedigree books that survey scholars quote and arrange marriages with the gift's inheritance in mind. Children are cup-tested young. A child with the sensitivity begins years of shards and blind tests under an older taster; a child without it usually trains at the survey bench or in the quarries. Trade custom protects the palate: tasters work mornings, rinse between lots, and eat the bland tasting-line diet before a grading shift.

encyclopedia.summary: Palate is an inherited Kyther sensitivity that distinguishes grades and veins of ringglass by the metallic trace they leave on the breath. Tasting families grade quarry lots, and their assay marks set the stock's price.
encyclopedia.title: Palate

affordances: A taster's breath is a portable assay office — grade, vein, and provenance called in seconds, trusted by the trade, and confirmable on the bench — which makes the tasting families' marks the range's working currency of trust.
cues: The taster breathes once across the bare shard, closes their eyes for a swallow's length, and says 'second grade, north vein — Ferren's quarry, upper gallery' into a silence full of money.
At the family bench, a blindfolded child works through a row of shards while an older taster records each answer beside the cup-test marks.
pressures: Palate fatigue accumulates across a shift, so a grading record includes the tasting order and the rinses taken between lots.
variations: Old family lines name tastes in a private vocabulary before translating for the buyer; survey-office tasters use catalog numbers from the first call.
Pedigree books record skipped inheritance as carefully as the gift, while cup tests direct training toward the tasting bench, survey instruments, or quarry work.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: A stiff gray film, cool and faintly pearly, cut to hand and market sizes with rounded salvage-shop corners. Written, it holds a dark clean line; wiped, it clears to gray with the faint ghost of old layers deep in the surface.
descriptiveIdentity.working: Any hard stylus marks it and a warm damp cloth wipes it, hundreds of times over. Deep-written marks settle in with the years, and a seasoned sheet carries its history as layered ghosts a strong lamp brings up.
descriptiveIdentity.risks: The ghosts are the hazard and the treasure: a wiped sheet testifies under a reading lamp, which has decided lawsuits, embarrassed ministries, and taught every trade in the system to burn its real secrets on paper.

facts.function: Reusable writing surface for working notes, postings, tallies, and lists
facts.grades: Graded by wipe count and surface: bright sheet wipes clean and true, seasoned sheet carries ghost layers, and blind sheet has gone glossy past marking
facts.availability: Salvage stock, cut and traded everywhere; the great sheet lodes are the ring's record offices, and cutting rights on a fresh office are priced like a small mine

sections.heading: Main
sections.text:
The everyday writing surface of the system came out of the ring's filing rooms. A palimpsest is elven record film — the working stationery of the ring's civil service, salvaged by the crate since the Famine years — and it does today what it did then: takes a hard stylus cleanly, shrugs off water, grease, and handling, and wipes back to gray with a warm cloth for the next use. A market stall chalks the morning prices on a board of it. A household keeps its lists on the kitchen sheet. A foreman's day rides in a hip pocket, wiped each night, and a family's sheets outlast the family's houses and pass down with the spoons.

Supply is salvage and the trade knows its lodes. The ring's record offices held sheet by the roomful, and cutting rights on a freshly opened office sell like claims on a small mine; the cut stock moves through salvage markets to the stationers, who trim, round the corners, and grade. Bright sheet wipes clean and true and prices highest. Seasoned sheet has taken decades of writing and carries ghost layers deep in the surface — faint strata of old marks that a strong reading lamp brings up — and blind sheet, gone glossy past marking, ends as tile and trim. The grading is by wipe: a stationer writes a test line, wipes, and reads what the surface kept.

sections.heading: Ghosts and What They Cost
sections.text:
The ghost layers give the material its second life and its legal career. A seasoned sheet is a shallow archive of everything it carried, recoverable in part under lamp and patience, and recovered ghosts are admissible where the custody holds — market disputes have turned on a wiped tally raised from a stall's own board, and one celebrated Verathi succession turned on a draft will its author wiped and its sheet remembered. The trades drew the working conclusion generations ago: routine business goes on sheet, and anything meant to vanish goes on paper, into the stove.

Archive houses buy seasoned sheet from famous rooms at ghost prices — stock from the ring's own offices carries elven working notes in its deep layers, and raising them is a recognized scholarly craft with its own journals and its own frauds. Lamp-readers work the middle of the market, hired to recover what a kitchen or workshop sheet remembers. Trade custom allows them to read the recovered words aloud only to the sheet's owner.

encyclopedia.summary: A palimpsest is the everyday reusable writing surface of the system: salvaged elven record film that takes a stylus mark, holds it through weather and handling, and wipes clean with a warm cloth for the next use. Markets chalk prices on it, households keep lists on it, and a family's sheets pass down like spoons.
encyclopedia.title: Palimpsest

affordances: A sheet is a lifetime of stationery in one object — write, wipe, write again through weather and grease — and a seasoned sheet's ghost layers make it a shallow archive that can testify about its own past under a reading lamp.
cues: The stall's price board is a pearly palimpsest chalk-marked in stylus, and between customers the seller wipes one line with a cloth kept warm on the kettle and writes the new price in its place.
Under the clerk's reading lamp, faint strata of older writing float up through the sheet's surface, and the clerk works down through them layer by layer, taking notes on paper.
pressures: The surface remembers what the wipe removes, so every sheet in a household or shop is a slow-burning record of its business — and the parties to any dispute know exactly which board to subpoena.
variations: Kitchen sheets and market boards run to seasoned stock and honest ghosts; courts and registries buy bright sheet by preference and retire it young, on principle.
Scholars pay lode prices for sheet cut from the ring's own offices, and the lamp-raising of elven working notes from deep layers is a recognized craft with journals, rivalries, and forgeries.

descriptiveIdentity.signs: A wall of soft dusk slides over the land at a walking cloud's pace — light dims, heat eases, gleeds brighten — and slides on, minutes later, restoring full day. On clear nights the same fragments cross as slow bright beads.
descriptiveIdentity.effects: Each settlement's almanac lists its passings to the breath: the long midday one for rest and hot-work, the pair of short morning ones the markets open between, the deep seasonal crossings the growers plant against.
descriptiveIdentity.hazards: A passing drops surface temperature and light together, and hot-country work planned into a passing must finish with it. Ashvane road records document severe heat injuries when crews remained mid-pour after full light returned.

facts.medium: Light and orbital shadow across the surface of Kaleidos
facts.nature: Orbital shadows of the larger surviving ring fragments, periodic and precisely predictable
facts.function: Surface settlements schedule work, rest, and growing cycles around the passing tables

sections.heading: Main
sections.text:
The intact ring cast one shadow, a steady band the old surface almanacs call the ribbon, and the surface lived under its single daily crossing. The broken ring casts many. The larger surviving fragments — the inhabited arcs, the great dead spans — cross Kaleidos's star on their orbits and send their shadows over the land as passings: minutes of moving dusk that arrive on schedule, to the breath, generation after generation. Light softens, heat eases, the gleeds brighten on glassy ground, and then full day slides back from the west edge of the shade.

Surface life is built to the passing tables. The long midday passing is the rest in hot country and the working window for heat-shy trades — glazing, wax work, the pouring of road surface on Ashvane's cousin-climates of the Avar summer. Markets open between the paired short passings of morning, and "first shade" and "second shade" are hours in every surface town's mouth. Growers plant to the deep seasonal crossings, when a great fragment's shadow returns day after day for a span of weeks and the fields under its track get a cooler season inside the season. A settlement's passing table is its first civic document; the almanac offices of Sithari print them for every registered town, and a town's copy, posted at the well or the market bell, is annotated in local hands until the next printing.

sections.heading: Shade Work and Shade Custom
sections.text:
A passing is a scheduled resource: cool light twice or thrice daily, priced into labor contracts through shade-work rates for jobs that use the shadow and full-light rates for jobs that avoid it. The shadow ends as punctually as it arrives. Ashvane and Avar crews drill a walk-away time before hot-country work begins, and working households mark overruns in the almanac margin.

Courting couples in the Sable Crescent walk the long passing. Kyther funerals time the lowering to a shade's arrival. Children race the shadow's western edge, a game also recorded in ring-era accounts of the ribbon.

encyclopedia.summary: Passings are the scheduled shadows of surviving ring fragments crossing the surface of Kaleidos — minutes of moving dusk that arrive to the almanac, structure the working day, and mark the sky's calendar in every surface settlement.
encyclopedia.title: Passings

affordances: A passing is scheduled cool and shade on open ground — the working window for heat-shy trades, the surface traveler's free rest stop, and a clock the whole countryside reads bare-eyed.
cues: A soft wall of dusk slides across the fields at a walking pace; workers straighten, markets pause mid-haggle, and the whole street's shadow arrives and leaves to the minute the posted table promised.
At the market bell hangs the town's passing table, printed in Sithari and annotated in three generations of local ink.
pressures: The shade ends to the minute, so work, travel, and meetings planned inside a passing inherit a fixed deadline; overruns in hot country expose people and materials to a rapid return of full heat.
variations: Fragment towns under a deep seasonal track get a cool growing season inside the season and plant a second crop against it; their neighbors a valley over, off the track, buy the surplus and resent the geometry.
The Sable Crescent walks its long passing for courtship and the Kyther valleys lower their dead to a shade's arrival, and both customs cite the other as the imported one.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: An ox-sized, round-backed shape moving at loam pace — a walking hill in bed-blue gray — on broad pads that leave prints glistening wet behind it, yesterday's prints already cured to dark glass.
descriptiveIdentity.behavior: It grazes the root mat on a lifelong circuit, laying resin with every step; the circuits crossing and re-crossing over years harden into the glazed trail networks, and the pavior keeps to its own trails with a settled preference that makes the networks roads.
descriptiveIdentity.threat: Its weight and steady pace make close footing dangerous; a harassed pavior continues along its circuit through fences, carts, and anyone trying to turn it.
descriptiveIdentity.senses: It reads the loam through its pads — moisture, root health, the beds' condition underfoot — and its circuit shifts track the ground's needs closely enough that the terraces read next season's bed plan off this season's trails.
descriptiveIdentity.risks: Cutting trail lacquer breaks the living cure and leaves a soft gap in the road. Terrace law therefore protects the paths, requires pavior gates in fences, and keeps traffic clear of an animal on its circuit.

facts.origin: Native to the blue-loam beds and coextensive with them; the terrace cultures' oldest land records already assume both
facts.biology: An ox-scaled, round-backed grazer on broad soft pads, feeding on the deep loam's root mat; the pads secrete a sealing resin with each step, and the resin cures in the loam's humid warmth — layer over layer, crossing over crossing — into a hard glazed surface
facts.lifespan: DUR60END; paviors keep lifelong circuits, and a matriarch's trail network is the work of decades
facts.function: Path-maker and bed-tender at once: the glazed trails firm the terraces' soft ground into all-weather roads, and the paviors' grazing keeps the root mat cropped in the rotation the beds need
facts.resonance_relation: The resin cures only in living loam, where the beds' damp warmth and faint band-murmur set it; resin removed from the beds stays gummy

sections.heading: Main
sections.text:
The blue-loam country's best roads are footprints. A pavior is an ox-sized, round-backed grazer on broad pads. Each pad lays resin into the damp root mat, where warmth and the bed's faint murmur cure it to blue-black glaze. One crossing leaves a line of dark coins; a season's circuit makes a track; a matriarch's decades of grazing rounds make a road network firm enough for carts. Resin cut from the bed stays gummy, so the useful surface remains attached to the living loam and to the animal that renews it.

Paviors keep lifelong grazing circuits through the same beds. They crop the root mat as they travel, rest on dry rises, and return to water and mineral licks along established branches. Terrace settlements build pavior gates into fences and plan rotations around those rounds. A circuit shift is also useful evidence: the pads respond to moisture and root condition, and gardeners compare a matriarch's new route with their bed surveys before laying out the next season.

Trail law treats the glazed paths as common way. Cutting lacquer breaks the cure and leaves a soft gap, while blocking a circuit brings a heavy animal steadily through the obstruction. The largest networks enter land records under the matriarch's name, her lifetime of crossings visible across several terraces.

encyclopedia.summary: Paviors are slow heavy grazers whose pads lay resin into the living blue loam. Repeated grazing circuits cure into the blue-black paths that carry terrace traffic across otherwise soft ground.
encyclopedia.title: Pavior

affordances: The trail networks are all-weather roads through ground that swallows boots, renewed by grazing and free at the price of custom — and the paviors' circuit shifts forecast bed condition ahead of any instrument.
cues: The morning's prints glisten wet down the terrace margin, yesterday's cured dark behind them, and the cart train swings onto the pavior's trail — the firmest road in the valley, renewed overnight by the roadbuilder grazing two beds over.
The bed council lays the survey beside the matriarch's new circuit; both show the same wet ground a season before planting.
variations: Matriarch networks carry the main cartage and enter the land records by name; young paviors' new circuits are watched with a prospector's interest, since a trail's first season predicts the road it will become.

The glaze itself varies bed to bed — deep-loam trails cure near-black and iron-hard, margin trails lighter and softer — and the terraces' road vocabulary grades cartage routes by the loam that cured them.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: Outwardly it could be anything — a converted cargo craft, survey hull, or old passenger kite — carrying one to four unmanned cutters in cradles. What marks a working Pell skiff is its repairs: scrape marks around a shutter, mismatched wall plates, a breaker moved within easier reach.
descriptiveIdentity.aboard: Short passages, heavy shutters, cleanable walls, exposed manual breakers, and painted deck routes showing which controls belong together. Each cutter has its own receiver, clock, and power break; closed rooms carry a physical tally outside the door naming who may reopen them. Cabins sit at the clean end past the bridge, and boots and outer clothing do not cross into them unwashed.
descriptiveIdentity.behavior: It stands off from the claim and takes material through remote cutters, each return landing in an isolated bay that is sounded and sampled before anything opens inward. A good cut looks uneventful from the bridge and exhausting in the process rooms. Returns sometimes carry living things — a cutter wake — and the response is to seal the room and kill every tone beyond it, because the intruder follows the strongest useful signal. Crews drop receivers and shear cutter lines before risking the route home.

facts.capacity: Three to twelve crew, one to four remote cutters, and isolated receiving rooms

sections.heading: Main
sections.text:
A Pell skiff is a salvage vessel built to receive material from unstable debris without bringing its crew alongside the claim. It carries one or more unmanned cutters, a separate receiver for each cutter, and enough processing rooms to decide what has come back before opening it to the rest of the ship. Ratters call almost every vessel they fly a skiff. The Pell pattern is the kind whose interior is arranged around doors that may need to close quickly.

Some Pell skiffs began as cargo craft, survey hulls, or old passenger kites. Others were built for remote work. Their outward forms vary. The repeated features are visible inside: short passages, heavy shutters, cleanable walls, exposed manual breakers, and instrument runs that do not share a clock.

sections.heading: The Receiving Side
sections.text:
A cutter couples a selected seam to the Pell skiff through Claim Coupling. The returned material enters an outer bay lined with replaceable plates. Loose dust settles first. Mechanical screens separate large stock from fragments that could reach a valve or door track. A second room receives useful material only after the outer bay has been sounded, sampled, and brought inside the skiff's pressure limits.

Each active cutter has its own receiver, clock, power break, and record. Painted routes on the deck show which controls belong together. The separation consumes space and cable, yet it prevents one coherent return from using the ship itself as a path into another claim. Crews adopted the layout after [Pell Four](/glass-frontier/entry/pell-four); shared clocks disappeared from licensed Pell skiffs within a season.

The shutters can be driven from the bridge and released by hand beside each opening. The hand wheel is slow because speed matters less than certainty after the powered system has given a false safe reading. A closed room carries a physical tally outside it: pressure, heat, field response, last entry, and the name of the person who may reopen it.

sections.heading: Working a Claim
sections.text:
A Pell skiff approaches only close enough to maintain a clear cutter path. The crew maps local debris, places retreat marks, and sounds the receiving rooms before launching anything. A Tuner chooses the seam response. A cutter operator flies the machine in, fixes the anchor head, and confirms that every return path ends in the intended bay. The deck lead's readback of the room state authorizes the tone.

Once material begins arriving, the vessel handles heat, pressure, waste, and resonance load that the claim no longer carries. The pilot keeps the skiff oriented while the receiving crew trims the flow. A good cut looks uneventful from the bridge and exhausting in the process rooms. The most valuable stock may arrive in minutes; cooling, separation, and cleaning can occupy the rest of the watch.

Crews treat cutters as expendable and protect the route home before the machine. A Pell skiff that drops a receiver, shears its cutter line, and leaves with empty holds may still have completed the job correctly.

sections.heading: Cutter Wakes
sections.text:
Remote returns sometimes carry living things. Deckmouths arrive in trapped pressure. Flintjacks follow active current. Small shear-jellies cling to loose material and open when the receiving atmosphere thickens. Crews call the intrusion a cutter wake and train for it as part of ordinary remote work.

The first response is to close the room and turn off every tone beyond it. Barriers and tuned deck weapons remain inside the bay, available without reopening the threatened door. A wake becomes difficult when a beast crosses into a shared service passage or when an operator keeps a downstream machine active. The intruder follows the strongest useful signal, which is often the equipment the crew most wants to save.

Older Pell skiffs are judged by how well they were rebuilt after wakes. Scrape marks around a shutter, mismatched wall plates, and a breaker moved within easier reach carry more information than a clean sales record.

sections.heading: A Small Working Vessel
sections.text:
A two-cutter Pell skiff usually carries a pilot, cutter operator, Tuner, deck lead, and two or three process hands. On a small crew those jobs overlap until the first live return, when every person must remain at one station. Larger skiffs add repair staff and separate watches rather than placing more people in the receiving line.

The crew lives close to the work. Cabins occupy the clean end of the hull beyond the bridge, with the galley and air plant between habitation and processing. Boots, tools, and outer clothing remain on the processing side until they have been washed and sounded, and the crossing rule is painted on the clean-end door.

Independent crews own many Pell skiffs outright or owe on them through a broker, yard, or flotilla debt. The [Pell Freight Assembly](/glass-frontier/entry/pell-freight-assembly) maintains shared receivers and finances rebuilds for its members. A skiff remains its crew's vessel under those arrangements. The Assembly can deny a berth to unsafe work; it does not take the helm.

encyclopedia.summary: A Pell skiff is a salvage vessel built to recover unstable debris without bringing its crew alongside the claim. Separate cutters, receivers, and processing rooms keep each return isolated until the crew knows what came back.
encyclopedia.title: Pell Skiff

affordances: The hand wheel and physical tally let a deck lead verify pressure, heat, field response, and last entry at the opening before releasing a room whose powered system has reported safe.
cues: Buyers, hirers, and berth masters read a Pell skiff's history off its repairs. Scrape marks around a shutter, mismatched wall plates, and a breaker moved within easier reach carry more about what the vessel has survived than its sales record does.
The repeated features are visible inside: short passages, heavy shutters, cleanable walls, exposed manual breakers, and instrument runs that do not share a clock.
pressures: Jobs overlap freely on a small Pell skiff until the first live return, and then pilot, cutter operator, Tuner, deck lead, and process hands are each fixed to one station. Anything needing a spare pair of hands while the tone runs costs whichever station is left empty.
variations: Converted cargo craft, survey hulls, and passenger kites keep their old outer silhouettes while gaining heavy shutters, exposed breakers, and isolated receiving bays inside.
Purpose-built Pell skiffs give every cutter its own receiver and clock, with the cabins past the bridge at the clean end of the vessel.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: A round furred body stands on small grasping paws; loose cheek folds puff outward during a greeting.
descriptiveIdentity.behavior: Peltri rub familiar objects across their cheeks, carry favored scraps to a sleeping hollow and invite play with a sideways hop.
descriptiveIdentity.senses: Scent distinguishes familiar people even when clothes or silhouettes change.
descriptiveIdentity.risks: An unfamiliar room can send a frightened animal into a warm inaccessible recess.

facts.biology: A compact furred omnivore with grasping forepaws, a balancing tail and soft scent-retaining folds along the cheeks
facts.principal_accommodation: Warm occupied rooms, varied food, companionship and covered sleeping places

sections.heading: Main
sections.text:
Peltri have traveled from Korvathi households into ship cabins and settlements across the system. The animal greets a familiar person by pushing its cheek folds against a hand, collecting the scents of places they have visited. It may then carry a glove to its sleeping hollow. A sideways hop and raised forepaws invite pursuit; a flattened body and tightly closed cheeks signal that the same approach has become frightening.

Many homes in [Oskara](/glass-frontier/entry/oskara) keep peltri, and some of the families with kin at [Outside](/glass-frontier/entry/outside) have sent young animals with returning visitors. Household versions differ in coat length, size and tolerance of strangers. A peltri recognizes a familiar scent beneath a changed face screen, which can be inconvenient at a private gathering. It can also greet a borrowed coat before discovering that the person inside it is a stranger.

In [Ithara](/glass-frontier/entry/ithara), peltri live entirely inside heated pressure rooms and ships. A child may know every household animal in one connected hall while never seeing an unprotected living thing outside. The [Ilvaren](/glass-frontier/entry/ilvaren) place abandoned peltri with households able to keep them company. Wealthy collectors favor elaborate long coats; working families often prefer short-coated animals that can be cleaned after a raid on the cooking shelves.

encyclopedia.summary: Peltri are small domesticated furred animals kept in Korvathi homes and traveling households, recognizing companions through scent rubbed onto their cheek folds.
encyclopedia.title: Peltri

affordances: Familiar scent can draw a peltri out of hiding or reveal that an apparently new visitor carries something belonging to a household friend.
cues: The small animal pushes a cheek fold into a visitor's glove, then carries the glove away when they loosen their grip.
A peltri bounds toward a borrowed coat and stops with its cheeks clamped shut when the wearer turns.
variations: Short-coated household lines tolerate busy rooms and spend much of the day following people.
Long-coated show lines require frequent grooming and often retreat to covered sleeping boxes during a noisy gathering.

sections.heading: Main
sections.text:
Eleven sapient species are documented in Kaleidos, and mixed-species settlements predate the Glassfall. Ring-era and early-colony records identify separate alien arrivals, elven bioengineering, and older native populations. The fae record remains disputed, and no surviving account connects every species to one origin.

The Peoples Register divides the eleven by population and institutional reach. The six major species anchor system-wide censuses, governments, and accords. Five smaller populations maintain institutions such as Kyther hold councils, outer route-hold libraries, and trellin keeper schools while appearing in mixed settlements throughout Kaleidos. *Minor* describes the Peoples Register's population class, not an individual's status or occupation. All eleven are person-scale, but their body plans vary considerably; kyrri, for example, have four lower limbs. The tables record only what current archives support.

sections.heading: Major Species
sections.text:
| Species | Origin | Resonance Relationship |
|---------|--------|------------------------|
| Elves | Native | Deeply attuned; primary ring-era resonance scientists |
| Humans | Alien | Learned through training and instruments |
| Orcs | Alien | Read most readily through material stress |
| Gnomes | Engineered | Directly sensed through ringglass-threaded biology |
| Fae | Engineered or extensively modified | Coherence aids help maintain bodily form |
| Dwarves | Alien | Fine signal vibration is legible through touch |

sections.heading: Minor Sapient Species
sections.text:
| People | Homeland | Resonance Relationship |
|--------|----------|------------------------|
| Heshari | The glass country | Learned; glass grade and stress read by bite and breath |
| Kyrri | The Kyther Range | Structural-band hearing through braced skeleton |
| Oruun | The spinways | Learned; local spin and trim felt through density-adaptive tissue |
| Trellin | Signal country | Native to the signal band through throat fans |
| Nacre | The outer route holds | Kinetic band recorded as groove structure in grown plates |

encyclopedia.summary: The Peoples Register records eleven sapient species: six large populations represented throughout the system's censuses and accords, and five smaller populations with their own civic institutions. Its tables summarize documented origins, homelands, and resonance relationships.
encyclopedia.title: The Peoples Register

affordances: The Peoples Register gives census offices and medical services a shared list of eleven peoples, their body plans, and their documented resonance relationships.
cues: The ferry queue runs the Peoples Register's length — a gnome's bones humming faintly in the quiet, an oruun turning a ring-weighted wrist, a kyrri braced comfortably on four limbs at the rail — and the clerk processes it all with one practiced glance apiece.
A census clerk records species where medicine, accommodation, or demographic totals require it; trade, residence, and civic standing are separate fields.
variations: Mixed-species settlement is the system's norm and predates the Glassfall — a port town's census runs the Peoples Register's whole length, and single-species communities are the exception the neighbors remark on.
The major-species table records disputed origins because surviving archives support that inquiry. The smaller-population table limits itself to documented homeland and resonance biology.

descriptiveIdentity.appearance: A tall pale wader with dove-gray plumage, a dark spear beak, and a deliberate high-stepping gait. Kept birds wear a household's leg ring.
descriptiveIdentity.behavior: The flock works the channels at first light and dusk, spearing vermin along the leech lines, and spends the day standing sentinel at the junctions — one bird per junction, by an arrangement the birds enforce themselves.
descriptiveIdentity.threat: A bird defending its junction strikes bare feet with the spear beak. Children learn the flock's spacing rules before entering the channels.
descriptiveIdentity.senses: The birds read the water first: Pickets abandoning a channel in a body is the gardens' oldest contamination alarm, and stewards close the reach on the flock's word alone.
descriptiveIdentity.risks: A flock bonds to its water rather than its keepers, and a household that moves learns the birds' opinion of the new channels by whether the flock follows.
